name: t3code
readme_content:
# T3 Code

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code)), [web app](https://app.t3.codes) and [Electron-based desktop app](https://t3.codes).

Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

## "Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

## Installation

> [!WARNING]
> T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, and fx. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:
>
> - Codex: install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`
> - Claude: install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`
> - Cursor: install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli) and run `agent login`
> - Grok Build: install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli) and run `grok login`
> - OpenCode: install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and run `opencode auth login`
> - Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use **Install Antigravity** and **Sign in with Google**. No CLI is required.
> - fx: install [fx](https://fx.sh) and run `fx login` on the machine running the T3 Code server ([setup guide](./docs/user/providers-fx.md))

### Command line

```bash
curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then run `t3` to start the server and open the local web app. `t3 service install` keeps it running in the background, `t3 update` moves to a newer release, and `t3 --help` has the full reference.

To try it once without installing, run `npx t3@latest` instead.

### Desktop app

Install the latest version of the desktop app from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), or from your favorite package registry:

#### Windows (`winget`)

```bash
winget install T3Tools.T3Code
```

#### Windows (`scoop`)

```bash
scoop install extras/t3code
```

#### macOS (Homebrew)

```bash
brew install --cask t3-code
```

#### Debian, Ubuntu (`.deb`)

Download the `.deb` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), then:

```bash
sudo apt install ./T3-Code-*.deb
```

#### Arch Linux (AUR)

Stable:

```bash
yay -S t3code-bin
```

Nightly:

```bash
yay -S t3code-nightly-bin
```

The AUR packaging is maintained in this repository under [`packaging/aur`](./packaging/aur).

#### Nix (nixpkgs)

```bash
nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code
```

The package is maintained in [nixpkgs](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/tree/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/t3/t3code)
and includes the desktop app (`t3code-desktop`) and the `t3` command.
See [Nix installation](./docs/user/install.md#nix-nixpkgs) for NixOS configuration and updates.

## Some notes

We are very very early in this project. Expect bugs.

We are (mostly) not accepting contributions yet. Small fixes may be considered. Big features will not be.

## Documentation

Full docs live in [docs/](./docs). There's no docs site yet.

- [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md)
- [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md)
- [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](./docs/user/keybindings.md)
- [Project settings](./docs/user/project-settings.md)
- [Appearance preferences](./docs/user/appearance.md)
- [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md)
- [Connect Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT and other agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md)
- [Keeping app and server in sync](./docs/user/updating.md)
- [Source control integrations](./docs/user/source-control.md)
- Multiple accounts: [Codex](./docs/user/providers-codex.md) · [Claude](./docs/user/providers-claude.md)
- [Run T3 Code as a background service](./docs/user/background-service.md)

Building from source? Start at [docs/internals/overview.md](./docs/internals/overview.md).

## If you REALLY want to contribute still.... read this first

### Install `vp`

T3 Code uses Vite+ so you'll need to install the global `vp` command-line tool.

#### macOS / Linux

```bash
curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash
```

#### Windows

```bash
irm https://vite.plus/ps1 | iex
```

Checkout their getting started guide for more information: https://viteplus.dev/guide/

### Install dependencies

```bash
vp i
```

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before reporting a bug or opening a PR.

Have a feature request? Start an [Ideas discussion](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas).

Need support? Join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv).

name: agent-desktop
description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
readme_content:
# agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree.

agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output, and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop status # platform, permissions, supported surfaces agent-desktop permissions --guide # macOS: walks you through the Accessibility grant ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable. On macOS and Linux, Homebrew also works: `brew install agent-desktop`. There is no official Scoop package yet. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. Release archives and building from source are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify ``` Each command prints one JSON envelope. A trimmed snapshot: ```json { "version": "2.6", "ok": true, "command": "snapshot", "data": { "app": "Finder", "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9", "ref_count": 59, "complete": true, "tree": { "role": "window", "name": "Downloads", "children": [ { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] } ] } } } ``` - **Refs belong to their snapshot.** A bare `@e8` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS`. When the UI changes, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: take a new snapshot and use its refs. - **Several windows** give `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`; `snapshot` lists the candidate window ids in `error.details`. Pass one with `--window-id`. - **Dense apps:** map first with `snapshot --skeleton --app Slack -i --compact`, then drill into one region with `snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact`. - **Headless by default.** Ref actions use the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus. The global `--headed` flag allows physical input. - **Post-action waits** observe the ref's original process. Window-owned refs stay pinned to their original window, including refs captured from a sheet, alert, popover, focused view, or Linux menu. macOS application menus keep their application-owned surface and need no document window. The wait reads the whole pinned window, so overlay selectors share its scope. [Wait scope and results](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/configuration#post-action-wait-flags) describe the selector limits. - `type`, `set-value`, and `clipboard-set` accept `--stdin` for piped text, keeping it out of process arguments. Run secret steps as separate commands; batch JSON text appears in process arguments. - **PowerShell.** Quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e8'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/quick-start). ## How it works Your agent calls the CLI, or the C library in process. Both run the same core, which reaches the OS only through `PlatformAdapter`. Each binary is built for one OS and talks to that OS's accessibility API. ## For AI agents The binary carries guides that match its version: ```bash agent-desktop skills get desktop # the loop, refs, verification and retry rules agent-desktop skills get platform # what differs on the OS you run on agent-desktop --help # flags for one command ``` Install the skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/agent-desktop): ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop ``` Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-desktop` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run `agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them. ``` Retry a failed command only when `error.disposition.retry` is `safe`. See [JSON output](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/json-output) for the envelope, error codes, and exit codes. ### MCP `agent-desktop mcp` serves every command as an MCP tool over stdio. A tool is named after its command (`desktop_snapshot`, `desktop_click`, `desktop_session_start`), takes that command's arguments, and returns its JSON envelope: ```json { "mcpServers": { "agent-desktop": { "command": "agent-desktop", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` Global flags given to `mcp`, such as `--session`, `--headed` or `--trace`, apply to every call. ## Commands agent-desktop has 60 command names, 56 operational commands. The other four (`key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up`) refuse to run until a daemon can release a held key or button. [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/commands) documents each one. | Group | Commands | |---|---| | Observe | `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` | | Act on a ref | `click`, `double-click`, `triple-click`, `right-click`, `type`, `set-value`, `clear`, `focus`, `select`, `toggle`, `check`, `uncheck`, `expand`, `collapse`, `scroll`, `scroll-to` | | Keyboard and mouse | `press`, `hover`, `drag`, `mouse-move`, `mouse-click`, `mouse-wheel`, `key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up` | | Apps and windows | `launch`, `close-app`, `list-apps`, `list-windows`, `list-displays`, `focus-window`, `resize-window`, `move-window`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `restore`, `open-system-surface` | | Notifications | `list-notifications`, `dismiss-notification`, `dismiss-all-notifications`, `notification-action` | | Clipboard | `clipboard-get`, `clipboard-set`, `clipboard-clear` | | Wait | `wait` | | Sessions | `session`, `trace`, `cursor-overlay` | | System | `status`, `permissions`, `version`, `batch`, `skills` | ## Platform support | Platform | Requirement | Accessibility API | |---|---|---| | [macOS](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/macos) | macOS 13 or later, Intel or Apple Silicon | AX API | | [Windows](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/windows) | Windows 10 1809 or later, x64 or ARM64 | UI Automation | | [Linux](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/linux) | Ubuntu 24.04 or later, x86_64 or aarch64, X11 or Wayland | AT-SPI | Each platform page lists what works headless, what needs `--headed`, and what refuses. ## C library Each release ships `libagent_desktop_ffi`, so a program can call agent-desktop in process. See the [C library docs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/ffi). ```python import ctypes lib = ctypes.CDLL("./lib/libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib") lib.ad_adapter_create.restype = ctypes.c_void_p lib.ad_adapter_destroy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p] assert lib.ad_init(7) == 0 # AD_RESULT_OK when the header's AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR matches the library adapter = lib.ad_adapter_create() lib.ad_adapter_destroy(adapter) ``` ## Development Each platform adapter builds only on its own OS, so scope cargo to the host's packages. On macOS: ```bash HOST_PKGS=(-p agent-desktop-core -p agent-desktop-macos -p agent-desktop -p agent-desktop-ffi) cargo test "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" cargo clippy "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings ``` On Windows, use `agent-desktop-windows` instead of `agent-desktop-macos`; on Linux, `agent-desktop-linux`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) lists every gate. ## Documentation - [Introduction](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop): what it is and how it works - [Snapshots and refs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/snapshots-and-refs) - [Errors and recovery](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/errors-and-recovery) - [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/skills) - [CONCEPTS.md](CONCEPTS.md): vocabulary - [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md) ## License Apache-2.0

[workspace]
members         = ["crates/core", "crates/macos", "crates/windows", "crates/linux", "crates/ffi", "src"]
default-members = ["crates/core", "crates/macos", "crates/windows", "crates/linux", "src"]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
edition      = "2024"
rust-version = "1.89"
license      = "Apache-2.0"
version      = "1.2.0"

[workspace.dependencies]
clap               = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive"] }
serde              = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json         = { version = "1.0", features = ["float_roundtrip"] }
thiserror          = "2.0"
tracing            = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter"] }
base64             = "0.23"
rustc-hash         = "2.1"
libc               = "0.2"
smallvec           = { version = "1.13", features = ["serde", "union"] }
agent-desktop-core = { path = "crates/core" }

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn = "warn"
unreachable_pub        = "allow"
unused_must_use        = "deny"
let_underscore_drop    = "allow"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
dbg_macro              = "deny"
todo                   = "warn"
needless_collect       = "warn"
redundant_clone        = "allow"
unwrap_used            = "allow"
expect_used            = "allow"
needless_pass_by_value = "allow"
manual_let_else        = "allow"
items_after_statements = "allow"
collapsible_if         = "allow"
print_stdout           = "allow"
print_stderr           = "allow"

[profile.release]
opt-level     = "z"
lto           = true
codegen-units = 1
strip         = true
panic         = "abort"

[profile.release.package.agent-desktop-core]
opt-level = 3

[profile.release.package.agent-desktop-macos]
opt-level = 3

[profile.ci]
inherits      = "release"
opt-level     = 1
lto           = false
codegen-units = 16
strip         = false
debug         = 1

[profile.release-ffi]
inherits = "release"
panic    = "unwind"

name: security-audit-skill
description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
readme_content:
# security-audit

A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in [Build your own vulnerability harness](https://blog.cloudflare.com/build-your-own-vulnerability-harness). The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

## What it does

The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

1. **Reconnaissance** -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in `architecture.md` and `coverage-ledger.json`.
2. **Coverage-led hunting** -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.
3. **Candidate validation** -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.
4. **Structured output** -- write `confirmed`, `needs_validation`, and `rejected` records to `findings.json` and validate them against `report-schema.json`.
5. **Independent record verification** -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.
6. **Target-neutral reporting** -- derive `REPORT.md`, `FINDINGS-DETAIL.md`, and `NEEDS-VALIDATION.md` from the verified records and coverage ledger.

The parent runs `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs `validate-findings.cjs` in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

The verdicts are distinct: `confirmed` has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, `needs_validation` has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and `rejected` records a disproved candidate.

Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `SKILL.md` | Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns |
| `RECONNAISSANCE.md` | Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions |
| `HUNTING.md` | Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules |
| `ATTACK-CLASSES.md` | Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts |
| `MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md` | Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets |
| `AI-AND-LLM.md` | Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets |
| `WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md` | HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets |
| `CLIENT-SIDE.md` | DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets |
| `SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md` | Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes |
| `CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md` | IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes |
| `PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md` | RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes |
| `RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md` | Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes |
| `DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md` | Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes |
| `DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md` | Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes |
| `VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md` | Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting |
| `report-schema.json` | JSON schema for all three `findings.json` verdicts |
| `validate-findings.cjs` | Zero-dependency validator for `findings.json` in Phases 4 and 5 |
| `validate-findings.test.cjs` | Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks |
| `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` | Zero-dependency validator for `coverage-ledger.json` in Phases 1–5 |
| `validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs` | Coverage-ledger validator tests |

## Installation

Install the skill with the [Skills CLI](https://skills.sh):

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
  --skill security-audit
```

Use `--global` for a user-level installation:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
  --skill security-audit \
  --global
```

Run `npx skills --help` for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

## Usage

Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

```
security audit this codebase
```

```
find security vulnerabilities in ./src
```

```
do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project
```

The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to `~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N>`. The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

## Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents
- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators
- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as `needs_validation` instead of executing target code.

## Design principles

- **Only confirm established boundary failures.** Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as `needs_validation` with its exact unresolved fact.
- **Adversarial validation.** The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.
- **Severity requires impact.** Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.
- **Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities.** If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.
- **Multiple runs improve coverage.** In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

## Contact

Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

name: skills
description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
readme_content:
# Skills For Real Engineers [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/mattpocock/skills)](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy. If you want to keep up with changes to these skills, and any new ones I create, you can join ~60,000 other devs on my newsletter: [Sign Up To The Newsletter](https://www.aihero.dev/s/skills-newsletter) ## Installation (30-second setup) A plugin updates itself. [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) copies editable files into your project, and you update them by hand. Pick one per agent, because installing both gives you every skill twice. ### 1. Get the skills
Claude Code ```bash claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official ``` Updates itself by default.
Codex ```bash codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Updates itself at startup.
GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code) ```bash copilot plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills copilot plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Then, once, add to `~/.copilot/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "mattpocock": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "mattpocock/skills" }, "autoUpdate": true } } } ``` In VS Code, run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source** and enter `https://github.com/mattpocock/skills`. It updates daily.
Gemini CLI (manual updates) ```bash gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/engineering gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/productivity ``` Re-run both commands to update.
Any other agent, or editable files (manual updates) ```bash npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a # cursor, opencode, devin, windsurf, amp, pi; omit -a to choose ``` When the installer asks which skills to take, include `setup-matt-pocock-skills`. To update, run `npx skills@latest update`, and re-run `add` to pick up new skills.
### 2. Run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` In your agent, run it once per repo. It will: - Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, GitLab, local files, or anything else you describe) - Ask you what labels you apply to tickets when you triage them (`/triage` uses labels) - Ask you where you want to save any docs we create ### 3. Bam - you're ready to go. ## Why These Skills Exist I built these skills as a way to fix common failure modes I see with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents. ### #1: The Agent Didn't Do What I Want > "No-one knows exactly what they want" > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**. The most common failure mode in software development is misalignment. You think the dev knows what you want. Then you see what they've built - and you realize it didn't understand you at all. This is just the same in the AI age. There is a communication gap between you and the agent. The fix for this is a **grilling session** - getting the agent to ask you detailed questions about what you're building. **The Fix** is to use: - [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md) - for non-code uses - [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md) - same as [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md), but adds more goodies (see below) These are my most popular skills. They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them _every_ time you want to make a change. ### #2: The Agent Is Way Too Verbose > With a ubiquitous language, conversations among developers and expressions of the code are all derived from the same domain model. > > Eric Evans, [Domain-Driven-Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Domain-Driven-Design-Tackling-Complexity-Software/dp/0321125215) **The Problem**: At the start of a project, devs and the people they're building the software for (the domain experts) are usually speaking different languages. I felt the same tension with my agents. Agents are usually dropped into a project and asked to figure out the jargon as they go. So they use 20 words where 1 will do. **The Fix** for this is a shared language. It's a document that helps agents decode the jargon used in the project.
Example Here's an example [glossary](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/blob/076a5a7a182db0fe1e62971dd7a68bcadf010f1c/CONTEXT.md) (still named `CONTEXT.md` at that pinned commit, from before the skills renamed the convention), from my `course-video-manager` repo. Which one is easier to read? - **BEFORE**: "There's a problem when a lesson inside a section of a course is made 'real' (i.e. given a spot in the file system)" - **AFTER**: "There's a problem with the materialization cascade" This concision pays off session after session.
This is built into [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md). It's a grilling session, but that helps you build a shared language with the AI, and document hard-to-explain decisions in ADR's. It's hard to explain how powerful this is. It might be the single coolest technique in this repo. Try it, and see. > [!TIP] > A shared language has many other benefits than reducing verbosity: > > - **Variables, functions and files are named consistently**, using the shared language > - As a result, the **codebase is easier to navigate** for the agent > - The agent also **spends fewer tokens on thinking**, because it has access to a more concise language ### #3: The Code Doesn't Work > "Always take small, deliberate steps. The rate of feedback is your speed limit. Never take on a task that’s too big." > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**: Let's say that you and the agent are aligned on what to build. What happens when the agent _still_ produces crap? It's time to look at your feedback loops. Without feedback on how the code it produces actually runs, the agent will be flying blind. **The Fix**: You need the usual tranche of feedback loops: static types, browser access, and automated tests. For automated tests, a red-green-refactor loop is critical. This is where the agent writes a failing test first, then fixes the test. This helps give the agent a consistent level of feedback that results in far better code. I've built a **[`/tdd`](./skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md) skill** you can slot into any project. It encourages red-green-refactor and gives the agent plenty of guidance on what makes good and bad tests. For debugging, I've also built a **[`/diagnosing-bugs`](./skills/engineering/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md)** skill that wraps best debugging practices into a disciplined loop, gated phase by phase. ### #4: We Built A Ball Of Mud > "Invest in the design of the system _every day_." > > Kent Beck, [Extreme Programming Explained](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Extreme-Programming-Explained-Embrace-Change/dp/0321278658) > "The best modules are deep. They allow a lot of functionality to be accessed through a simple interface." > > John Ousterhout, [A Philosophy Of Software Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Philosophy-Software-Design-2nd/dp/173210221X) **The Problem**: Most apps built with agents are complex and hard to change. Because agents can radically speed up coding, they also accelerate software entropy. Codebases get more complex at an unprecedented rate. **The Fix** for this is a radical new approach to AI-powered development: caring about the design of the code. This is built in to every layer of these skills: - [`/to-spec`](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md) quizzes you about which modules you're touching before creating a spec And crucially, [`/improve-codebase-architecture`](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md) surveys a codebase for deepening opportunities and hands you the candidates. I recommend running it on your codebase once every few days. It is a survey, not a rescue: on a genuinely old codebase it will find real candidates, but it won't untangle the mud for you. ### Summary Software engineering fundamentals matter more than ever. These skills are my best effort at condensing these fundamentals into repeatable practices, to help you ship the best apps of your career. Enjoy. ## Reference These split on one axis: who can invoke them. **User-invoked** skills are reachable only when you type them (e.g. `/grill-me`); their job is to orchestrate. **Model-invoked** skills can be invoked by you _or_ reached for automatically by the agent when the task fits; they hold the reusable discipline. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, but never another user-invoked one. ### Engineering Skills I use daily for code work. **User-invoked** - **[ask-matt](./skills/engineering/ask-matt/SKILL.md)**: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the user-invoked skills in this repo. - **[grill-with-docs](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md)**: Grilling session that also builds your project's domain model, sharpening terminology and updating `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs inline. - **[triage](./skills/engineering/triage/SKILL.md)**: Move issues through a state machine of triage roles. - **[improve-codebase-architecture](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md)**: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick. - **[setup-matt-pocock-skills](./skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md)**: Configure this repo for the engineering skills (issue tracker, triage labels, domain doc layout). Run once per repo before using the other engineering skills. - **[to-spec](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md)**: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker. No interview, just synthesizes what you've already discussed. - **[to-tickets](./skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md)**: Break any plan, spec, or conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, written as text in a local file, or as native blocking links on a real tracker. - **[implement](./skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md)**: Build the work described by a spec or set of tickets, driving `/tdd` at pre-agreed seams and closing out with `/code-review` before committing. - **[implement-spec](./skills/engineering/implement-spec/SKILL.md)**: Implement a whole spec on one integration branch. Works the tickets as a task graph, runni

name: auto-ontology
description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.
readme_content:
# Auto Ontology Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own. It enables developers to: - Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs. - Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems. - Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer. - Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with every question. ## Benchmarks To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to the [ontology SQL evaluation repository](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ontology-sql-eval/). > **Licensing & contributions.** Auto Ontology is distributed under the > [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). Third-party open-source components > bundled, linked, or otherwise used by this project are listed in > [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). **This project > is currently not accepting external contributions.**

## Key Features - **Natural-language querying** of structured data — questions are translated to SQL and executed against connected databases, powered by NVIDIA NIM. - **Semantic catalog / ontology layer** over relational sources, stored in Postgres alongside the catalog it describes. - **Authentication & RBAC** —using [Better Auth](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth). - **Web UI** for chat, analysis, data catalog, analytics, and settings. - **Flexible deployment** — Helm chart for Kubernetes or Docker Compose for a local stack. ## Software Components | Component | Technology | Role | Default port | | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------ | | Frontend | Next.js 16 (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4), Better Auth, Prisma | Web UI, authentication, API gateway | 3000 | | Backend | FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain | Chat / NL-to-SQL, catalog, datasource APIs | 3001 | | Ingestion worker | FastAPI (Python 3.12+) | Ingests tabular data and writes embeddings | 3002 | | Postgres + pgvector | Relational Database | App metadata, the catalog and ontology, vector store | 5432 | | HashiCorp Vault | Optional | Secure storage of connection credentials | — | ### NVIDIA NIM Auto Ontology uses NVIDIA NIM endpoints for inference — either the hosted [NVIDIA API catalog](https://build.nvidia.com) (`integrate.api.nvidia.com`) or self-hosted NIMs. The defaults in `.env.example` are: - **LLM:** `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` - **Embeddings:** `nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b` - **Reranking:** `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2` The endpoints and models are configured via the `DEFAULT_MODELS_ENDPOINT`, `DEFAULT_MODELS_MODEL`, `EMBED_ENDPOINT`, and `EMBED_MODEL` environment variables and require a `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. #### Model triplets Each model role is configured by a **triplet** of environment variables — `_ENDPOINT` (URL), `_API_KEY`, and `_MODEL`: | Prefix | Role | | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `DEFAULT_MODELS` | Shared default; every field below falls back to it. | | `REASONING` | Main chat / NL-to-SQL model. | | `NON_REASONING` | Lighter model used for entity extraction. | | `EMBED` | Text-embedding model (must match between ingest and query). | | `RERANK` | Reranker used by the retrieval flow. | You can set a full triplet, only some of its fields, or none at all — any field left unset falls back to the matching `DEFAULT_MODELS_`. So the simplest setup is to fill in `DEFAULT_MODELS_*` and override per-triplet fields only where they differ (e.g. `EMBED_MODEL`, `NON_REASONING_MODEL`). `*_API_KEY` also falls back to the legacy `NVIDIA_API_KEY` for backward compatibility. ## Quickstart This runs Auto-Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers, Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and an NVIDIA API key (`nvapi-...`) from [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com). 1. Clone the repository and create `.env`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology cp .env.example .env ``` Then set these values in `.env`: ```dotenv DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY=nvapi-... AUTH_SECRET= APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 POSTGRES_PASSWORD= CONNECTION_STRINGS=postgresql://postgres:@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD= PGADMIN_PASSWORD= ``` Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace each default password before you start it. `.env.example` also sets an API key per model role: replace each `nvapi-your-api-key-here` with your key, or delete those lines so they fall back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. 2. Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set: ```bash docker compose up -d --wait postgres git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval (cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \ POSTGRES_PASSWORD='' \ uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop) ``` 3. Build and start the rest of the stack: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` 4. Open and sign in with `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Go to **Settings → Semantic Compilation** and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts immediately and reports **Semantic compilation is ready** when it finishes. 5. Ask a question in **Chat**: > What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania > in June 2015? The agent resolves *revenue*, *product*, and *state* to terms in the ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it, so you can check the result against the source: ```text Answer: Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines. SQL: SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines FROM sales.invoicelines il JOIN sales.invoices i ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid JOIN warehouse.stockitems si ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid JOIN sales.customers c ON i.customerid = c.customerid JOIN application.cities ct ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll' AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania' AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01' Steps: Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province Validated the filter values against the data, then executed ``` 6. Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve against. An agent connected through [MCP](#mcp-server) checks answerability first and asks you to clarify: ```text You: What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015? Agent: check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend" Agent: I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another source I should connect? ``` If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for `localhost:3000` and sign in again. For other setup failures, see the [setup skill's troubleshooting guide](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/references/troubleshooting.md). ## How it works

Auto-Ontology works in three stages: it generates an ontology, people certify it, and the agent answers questions from it. The ontology holds three kinds of definition: - **Terms.** Business concepts such as *Customer* or *Invoice Line*, each with a description and synonyms, mapped to the columns that hold them. - **SQL attributes.** Reviewed SQL expressions under a term, such as a margin or a rolling total. The agent reuses them, so answers compute each measure the same way. - **Relationships.** How tables join, including bridge tables, inferred from keys and from the data. **Generate.** The ingestion service builds a first draft from the source databases: 1. Read sources: extract schemas, profile columns, and sample values into the catalog. 2. Name entities: extract terms table by table and map each to columns. 3. Resolve relationships: infer joins between tables and bridge tables, and suggest SQL attributes from query history. 4. Write the ontology: store terms, relationships, and SQL attributes in Postgres, with embeddings in pgvector for retrieval. The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting **Order** shows its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

**Certify.** People make the draft trustworthy: 1. Test with real questions in Chat, or with `check_answerable` and `ask_question` over MCP. 2. Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API. 3. Certify names, descriptions, and SQL attributes once they're correct. **Answer.** For each question, the agent: 1. Classifies the intent and extracts the entities the question names. 2. Retrieves candidate terms, columns, and SQL attributes by embedding search. 3. Writes SQL from those

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES.
# All rights reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

[project]
name = "auto-ontology-server"
version = "1.2.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.14"
dependencies = [
    "duckdb>=1.5.5",
    "fastapi>=0.141.1",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    "hvac>=2.4.0",
    # Capped at 1.3.4, the last release that accepts openai<2.45.0; see the openai pin.
    "langchain-openai>=1.3.0,<1.3.5",
    "langgraph>=1.2.11",
    "pydantic>=2.13.5",
    # Kept below 3 until the code is tested against pandas 3; the cap used to be
    # forced by nemo-retriever.
    "pandas>=2.3.3,<3",
    "psycopg-pool>=3.3.1",
    "psycopg[binary]>=3.3.4",
    "pyheavydb>=8.0.1.post1",
    # `heavydb/version.py` does `import importlib_metadata` -- the backport, not
    # the stdlib `importlib.metadata` -- but pyheavydb does not declare it. It
    # used to arrive transitively; an upgrade dropped whatever was carrying it
    # and every `import auto_ontology.connectors` started failing at collection. Declared
    # here so the next upgrade cannot take it away again.
    "importlib-metadata>=8.7.1",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.3",
    "snowflake-connector-python>=4.7.2",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.52.4",
    # The pyarrow extra turns on Arrow result sets and cloud fetch; without it
    # large Databricks reads fall back to slow row-by-row Thrift fetches.
    "databricks-sql-connector[pyarrow]>=4.4.0",
    "mysql-connector-python>=26.7.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0.52",
    "alembic>=1.19.1",
    "apache-ossie-nvidia-auto-ontology @ git+https://github.com/apache/ossie-converters.git@cb4b46b97bcdb9f2685ef2f7023b9134a4426da2#subdirectory=nvidia",
    "langchain-postgres>=0.0.17",
    "pyhive[hive-pure-sasl]>=0.7.0",
    "thrift>=0.24.0",
    "thrift-sasl>=0.4.3",
    "pure-sasl>=0.6.2",
    "pyjks>=20.0.0",
    "trino>=0.339.0",
    # The embedding client (auto_ontology/utils/embedding.py). Pinned to the
    # version nemo-gym 0.6.0 declares, so this matches the ontology-sql-eval
    # harness.
    "openai==2.44.0",
    # Imported directly but previously only installed transitively. Declared so
    # dropping whatever carried them cannot break an import the way pyheavydb's
    # importlib-metadata did; langchain-nvidia-ai-endpoints arrived solely via
    # nemo-retriever.
    "langchain-nvidia-ai-endpoints>=1.4.3",
    "langchain-core>=1.6.1",
    "sqlglot>=30.17.0",
    "numpy>=2.5.2",
    "requests>=2.34.2",
    "tqdm>=4.70.0",
    "cryptography>=50.0.1",
    # Not imported, but FastAPI refuses to register the model-import upload
    # route without it.
    "python-multipart>=0.0.32",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
kumo = ["kumo-relational-client[relational]>=1.0.0,<2"]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["auto_ontology"]

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.uv]
package = true
# Patched versions of transitive dependencies flagged by nSpect. Constraints,
# so their dependents' upper bounds still apply.
constraint-dependencies = [
    "pyjwt>=2.15.1",  # BDSA-2026-35552 (via databricks/snowflake connectors)
    "urllib3>=2.8.0",  # BDSA-2026-35861, BDSA-2026-35864 (via requests, botocore)
]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "vendored-engine"
url = "vendor/wheels"
format = "flat"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=9.1.1",
    "ruff>=0.16.5",
]
release = [
    "ngcsdk>=4.37.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
]

# Stated, not inherited. With no `select` at all, the rule set is whatever the
# installed ruff happens to default to -- and 0.16 widened that default from
# `E4,E7,E9,F` to some twenty families (B, BLE, S, SIM, TRY, UP, ...), turning a
# routine version bump into 541 findings in code nobody had touched.
#
# These are the rules the codebase was written against and passes cleanly. The
# wider set is worth adopting deliberately, as its own change: a good part of it
# argues with patterns that are intentional here -- BLE001 and S110 against the
# best-effort `except Exception` around reads whose failure is meant to
# degrade rather than raise, for instance -- so it needs judgement per rule, not
# a bulk `--fix`.
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
# mcp/ is a separate project with its own venv and CI workflow. It must stay out
# of this suite: pythonpath = ["."] would otherwise make the mcp/ directory
# shadow the installed mcp SDK as a namespace package.
addopts = "--import-mode=importlib --ignore=mcp"

name: Scrapling
description: 🕷️ The BEST Web Scraping framework that handles everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl! Don't be shy, join here: https://discord.gg/EMgGbDceNQ and follow here for daily tips and tricks: https://x.com/Scrapling_dev
readme_content:
Effortless Web Scraping for the Modern Web





Selection methods · Fetchers · Spiders · Proxy Rotation · CLI · MCP

Scrapling is a Python Web Scraping framework that brings fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, powerful parsing, and concurrent crawling into one library. Scrape static pages, render JavaScript, interact with websites, and extract data from the API calls behind them. Build crawlers with reusable sessions, proxy rotation, automatic retries, pause/resume, and built-in data exports. Use it from Python, the terminal, or your AI agent through its MCP server and Agent Skill. From extracting a few fields to collecting a whole website as clean Markdown, Scrapling covers the full scraping workflow. ## What you can do with Scrapling - **[Fetch & interact](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/fetching/choosing.html)**: Fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, JavaScript rendering, Cloudflare Turnstile/Interstitial handling, persistent sessions, and background API capture. - **[Parse & extract](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/parsing/selection.html)**: CSS, XPath, text and regex search, adaptive element tracking, similar-element matching, and clean Markdown output. - **[Crawl & export](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/spiders/getting-started.html)**: Concurrent spiders, proxy rotation, retries, AutoThrottle, pause/resume, streaming, ready-made templates, and JSON/JSONL/CSV/XML exports. - **[Scrape with AI or from your terminal](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ai/mcp-server.html)**: An MCP server for AI agents to browse and extract data, an Agent Skill, CLI commands, and an interactive shell. Start with a single page: ```python from scrapling.fetchers import Fetcher page = Fetcher.get('https://quotes.toscrape.com/') quotes = page.css('.quote .text::text').getall() print(quotes) ``` Or scale up with a spider: ```python from scrapling.spiders import Spider, Response class QuotesSpider(Spider): name = "quotes" start_urls = ["https://quotes.toscrape.com/"] async def parse(self, response: Response): for quote in response.css('.quote'): yield { "text": quote.css('.text::text').get(), "author": quote.css('.author::text').get(), } result = QuotesSpider().start() print(len(result.items)) result.items.to_json("quotes.json") ``` This prints `10` and saves the quotes and authors to `quotes.json`.

name: impeccable
description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.
readme_content:
# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### 24 commands | | Commands | |---|---| | **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects | | **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report | | **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states | | **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking | | **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system | The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the `codex` CLI from your PATH instead (or `claude` when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set `IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat` in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or `off` to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup. ## Three ways to run the detector **In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks). **In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent: ```bash npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description ``` Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`. Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: ``. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay). ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to ge

name: claude-mem
description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
readme_content:
🇨🇳 中文 • 🇹🇼 繁體中文 • 🇯🇵 日本語 • 🇵🇹 Português • 🇧🇷 Português • 🇰🇷 한국어 • 🇪🇸 Español • 🇩🇪 Deutsch • 🇫🇷 Français • 🇮🇱 עברית • 🇸🇦 العربية • 🇷🇺 Русский • 🇵🇱 Polski • 🇨🇿 Čeština • 🇳🇱 Nederlands • 🇹🇷 Türkçe • 🇺🇦 Українська • 🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt • 🇵🇭 Tagalog • 🇮🇩 Indonesia • 🇹🇭 ไทย • 🇮🇳 हिन्दी • 🇧🇩 বাংলা • 🇵🇰 اردو • 🇷🇴 Română • 🇸🇪 Svenska • 🇮🇹 Italiano • 🇬🇷 Ελληνικά • 🇭🇺 Magyar • 🇫🇮 Suomi • 🇩🇰 Dansk • 🇳🇴 Norsk

Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it.


Quick Start • How It Works • Search Tools • Documentation • Configuration • Troubleshooting • License

Every new session, your agent starts from zero. It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together.

Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents. Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code and Warp can search your memory, but their sessions aren't recorded.

--- ## Quick Start **Installing for someone as an AI agent?** Run `npx claude-mem install --runtime worker` on their computer in an interactive terminal (enable PTY in your shell tool). It first asks in the terminal which agents to set up and, for Claude Code, whether to disable native auto-memory (and whether to overwrite an existing install). Relay each question to the user and type their answer, or pass `--ide ` to skip the first one. Keep the installer running. When it prints **Continue setup in your browser**, open that URL in the user's browser if the installer hasn't already opened it. Let the user go through setup and make their own choices, including the usage-analytics question the installer may ask at the end. If you can't run an interactive terminal on their computer, give them the command to run locally. ```bash npx claude-mem install ``` The installer finds the agents on your machine and asks which ones to set up. Then just start working: observations stream in from your first prompt, and your second session in a project opens with memory from the first. (Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code and Warp get memory search only, so their sessions don't add to it.) The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link, no card required to sign in). Choosing the **claude-mem observer** then starts its **30 Day Free Trial** on a checkout page that asks for a payment method; once it completes, the installer saves your memory key. With the observer, memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider: the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Your memory lives in `~/.claude-mem` on your machine. Cloud sync is opt-in. Anonymous usage analytics are on by default; `npx claude-mem telemetry disable` turns them off ([what's collected](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/telemetry)). Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem /plugin install claude-mem ``` Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions. > **Note:** Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but `npm install -g claude-mem` installs the **SDK/library only** — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via `npx claude-mem install` or the `/plugin` commands above. ### Other agents `npx claude-mem install` covers every supported agent. To set up one agent directly, pass `--ide`. **OpenCode** (1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2). Restart OpenCode after installing. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide opencode ``` **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers). The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide t3code ``` **Antigravity CLI** ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity ``` **OMP (Oh My Pi):** ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide omp ``` **Pi and DeepSeek Harness** use the worker runtime. See [native harness setup](docs/native-harness-integrations.md) for capture, recall, and troubleshooting. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide pi npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui ``` **Grok Bot:** see [Grok Bot](#grok-bot) below. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` The full list of `--ide` values is in `npx claude-mem --help`. #### Grok Bot Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. **Opt-in awareness push:** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Enable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=true` and set `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_AGENT_IDS` to your agent UUIDs (empty by default). #### 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) gateways with a single command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash ``` The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the [OpenClaw Integration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/openclaw-integration) for details. ## What You Get - 🧠 **The next session starts where the last one left off.** Each session opens with a compact index of past observations, layered so the agent opens full details only when it needs them, and the header can show what each layer costs in tokens. - 🔍 **Find anything you worked on.** The mem-search skill searches your project history in three steps (index, timeline, details), so the agent spends tokens only on what it opens. - 🖥️ **Watch it work, and keep track of yours.** My Work shows live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. [Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai

name: OpenMausBot
description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use
readme_content:
# OpenMausBot **The open-source Grok Bot alternative: your own team of AI bots, in a chat app.** [**openmausbot.com**](https://www.openmausbot.com)  ·  [Download](https://www.openmausbot.com/download)  ·  [Open source Grok Bot alternative, compared](https://www.openmausbot.com/blog/grok-bot-vs-openmausbot) OpenMausBot is an open-source Grok Bot alternative: an independent project inspired by **Grok Bot**, and the open-source alternative to **Meta Muse**, **OpenAI dots** and **Cue by Manus** — bring-your-own-agent, local-first, on the models you already have. Also known as **MausBot**; formerly **OpenGrokBot**. Not affiliated with xAI, Meta, OpenAI or Manus. Every bot in the sidebar is a real agent — Claude or Codex running locally under the hood — with its own personality, its own model, its own cloud computer, and its own connected apps. Talk to them like contacts. Watch them work. Approve what matters. ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-strict-3178C6?logo=typescript&logoColor=white) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-19-61DAFB?logo=react&logoColor=black) ![Electron](https://img.shields.io/badge/Electron-macOS%20%C2%B7%20Windows%20%C2%B7%20Ubuntu-2B2E3A?logo=electron&logoColor=9FEAF9) ![Agents](https://img.shields.io/badge/agents-Claude%20·%20Codex-d97757) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/milind-soni/OpenMausBot?label=release&color=1084fe&cacheSeconds=300)](https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot/releases/latest) ![PRs](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-38d591)
      [latest release](https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot/releases/latest)  ·  macOS: Apple silicon & Intel · signed & notarized .dmg  ·  Windows: x64 installer  ·  Ubuntu 24.04 x64: .deb or AppImage beta  ·  [all releases](https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot/releases)


Powered by boat.dev


--- > ⚠️ **No affiliation with any cryptocurrency.** OpenMausBot has no token. Any coin using the OpenMausBot, Maus, or SupaMaus name is not created, endorsed, or affiliated with this project or its maintainer. I have received no tokens, payment, or allocation from anyone, and I will not be endorsing any token. ## Why One assistant in one box is the wrong shape for agents. OpenMausBot is an independent, open-source project inspired by **Grok Bot** — it keeps the idea (AI as a *messaging app*: a roster of bots you chat with, each with its own personality, memory of its thread, model, computer, and apps) and rebuilds it open, local-first, and on the agents you already have: - **Bring your own agents.** Bots run on the `claude`, `codex`, and `grok` CLIs installed on your own machine — your existing logins and subscriptions, no new accounts, no proxy in the middle. Point any engine at a custom CLI binary (a versioned build or wrapper) in **Settings → Engines**. - **Local first.** One small harness server on `127.0.0.1` owns every agent process. Transcripts, keys, and events live in `~/.openmausbot`, not a cloud. - **Agents with hands.** Each bot can use a cloud Linux desktop, an isolated Local VM, or—where the platform safety boundary is currently certified—your own computer, plus 500+ apps through Composio. Host control is available on macOS and Ubuntu Xorg after explicit opt-in. Ubuntu Wayland host control remains disabled while issue #345 is resolved. ## The open-source alternative to Grok Bot, Muse, dots and Cue Four closed personal-agent products shipped in seven weeks of 2026, and each one keeps the model, the computer and your data on its maker's side of the line. OpenMausBot is the open-source version of that shape: a team of agents in a chat app, each with its own model, its own computer and its own connected apps, running on your machine under Apache 2.0. If you searched for an *open Muse*, *open dots*, an *open-source Grok Bot*, an *open Instinct* or an *open Cue*, this is the repository. | Looking for | What it is | How OpenMausBot differs | Read more | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Open source Grok Bot** | xAI's roster of bots on one shared cloud computer, Grok only, from a SuperGrok or Cursor plan | Same roster shape; any model per bot; your own machine; approval cards | [Grok Bot vs OpenMausBot](https://www.openmausbot.com/blog/grok-bot-vs-openmausbot) | | **Open Muse** | Meta's single personal agent in a Meta cloud VM, US and Canada only | A team instead of one agent; runs anywhere; data in `~/.openmausbot` | [Meta Muse alternative](https://www.openmausbot.com/blog/open-source-alternative-to-meta-muse) | | **Open dots** | OpenAI's always-on agent inside ChatGPT, GPT only, Pro and Business Premium plans | Several agents; your Claude, ChatGPT or Grok login; no plan required | [OpenAI dots alternative](https://www.openmausbot.com/blog/openai-dots-alternative) | | **Open Cue** | Manus's invite-only agents with their own phone, email and wallet | No invite; OAuth instead of passwords; open source | [Cue by Manus alternative](https://www.openmausbot.com/blog/open-source-alternative-to-cue-by-manus) | | **Open Instinct** | Spear Street's invite-only agent that holds your passwords on a cloud computer | Ask for approval when you want it; signs in over OAuth; your machine | [Instinct AI alternative](https://www.openmausbot.com/blog/instinct-ai-alternative) | All five side by side: [Muse vs Grok Bot vs Dots vs Cue](https://www.openmausbot.com/blog/muse-vs-grok-bot-vs-dots-vs-cue), and a decision guide in five questions: [Which AI agent should I use?](https://www.openmausbot.com/blog/which-ai-agent-should-i-use) ## Features
### 🧠 Pick a brain per bot A model picker with a provider rail — Claude and Codex models side by side, defaults marked, unavailable providers dimmed with the reason. Switch a bot's model mid-conversation. ### 🖥️ Every bot gets a computer Open the Computer panel and the bot's cloud desktop spins up on its own — live screen preview while it works, "Open desktop" to take over in your browser, or point the bot at *this Mac* instead.
### 🙋 Bots ask before they act Shell commands, file edits, and questions surface as inline cards — Allow / Deny / answer in chat. A permission broker turns every risky action into a decision you make, for cloud and local computers alike. ### 🔌 Connected apps A one-click marketplace over Composio Sessions: Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear and hundreds more. OAuth once, and every bot can use them as tools.
### 🗂 Manage bots like chats Right-click any bot: pin, mark unread, edit profile, duplicate, copy conversation ID, hide, delete. It's a messaging app — your agents behave like contacts. ### 🔑 Keys once, everything lights up Paste credentials in App Settings — they persist locally and the provider fleet hot-reloads instantly. Secrets are write-only: the UI only ever sees "configured" flags.
### #️⃣ Channels for every context Keep Work, Personal, and each project in separate channels without cloning your bots. Every channel has its own transcript, shared instructions, working folder, responder rules, and editable bot roster. File a channel and its bots under a named context, then rename it or change its members whenever the team changes. ### ⚡ Fast decisions with Jev Add a Cloudflare Workers AI token with its account ID, a TypeSafe Jev key, or an OpenRouter key and model, in **Settings → Decision and extraction** and rooms set to **Auto** pick the bot that fits each un-mentioned message in a few hundred milliseconds, falling back to the room's lead whenever the decision model is off or unsure. See [docs/decision-model.md](docs/decision-model.md). ### 📦 Install a complete team from one Markdown file Browse outcome-driven teams on [BotMRR](https://botmrr.io), then choose **Add to OpenMausBot**. The app opens a review screen before creating the bots, Chief of Staff, channels, playbooks, connector checklist, and suggested routines. You can also import the same `.md` file from disk or paste its public GitHub URL in **Teams → Import**. The format stays portable: OpenMausBot reads the structured YAML frontmatter for a reliable one-click install, while Grok, Claude, ChatGPT, and people can follow the ordinary Markdown playbook. Connections remain off until you approve them, routines arrive paused, and packages never carry credentials, conversations, permissions, memory, or computer access. Browse the [open-source playbook repository](https://github.com/milind-soni/openmausbot-teams) or read its [portable format](https://github.com/milind-soni/openmausbot-teams/blob/main/FORMAT.md). ### 🤝 Share a whole department Right-click a department and choose **Share department…** (or use **Templates → Share**) to save the whole department as one file: its bots with their instructions, pictur
