[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools==84.0.0", "wheel==0.48.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "pr-agent"
version = "0.49.0"

authors = [
  { name = "QodoAI", email = "ofir.f@qodo.ai" },
]

maintainers = [
  { name = "Naor Peled", email = "me@naor.dev" },
  { name = "Ofir Friedman", email = "ofir.f@qodo.ai" },
]

description = "PR-Agent aims to help efficiently review and handle pull requests, by providing AI feedback and suggestions."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
keywords = ["AI", "Agents", "Pull Request", "Automation", "Code Review"]
license = { file = "LICENSE" }

classifiers = [
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
]
# Exact versions for this repo's own builds (Docker, CI, uv sync) come from
# uv.lock. Security-sensitive packages generally declare >=patched,<next-major
# ranges instead of == pins so pip consumers can pull security patches on
# their own cadence (#2523); the floor is the last vetted patched release.
# Keep certifi's calendar-versioned CA updates unbounded rather than
# treating a new year as an API-major compatibility boundary.
dependencies = [
  "aiohttp>=3.14.3,<4",
  "anthropic>=0.69.0",
  "certifi>=2026.10.23",
  "dynaconf>=3.3.5,<4",
  "fastapi>=0.141.1,<1",
  "GitPython>=3.1.62,<4",
  "starlette>=1.6.0,<2",
  "Jinja2==3.1.6",
  "litellm==1.105.1",
  "loguru==0.7.3",
  "openai>=1.55.3",
  "PyJWT>=2.15.1,<3",
  "PyYAML==6.0.3",
  "starlette-context==0.5.1",
  "tiktoken==0.14.0",
  "ujson>=5.13.0,<7",
  "unidiff==1.0.1",
  # Declare urllib3 directly because gerrit_provider.py imports urllib3.util; the >=2.8.0
  # floor is a security requirement and follows the >=patched,<next-major convention above.
  "urllib3>=2.8.0,<3",
  "uvicorn>=0.36.0,<1",
  "uvicorn-worker==0.4.0",
  "tenacity==8.2.3",
  "langfuse==4.18.0",
  "gunicorn==26.2.0",
  "pydantic==2.14.2",
  # LiteLLM declares pydantic-settings as a base dependency and imports it unconditionally from
  # litellm/integrations/otel/model/config.py. Keep the exact pin to lock the resolved transitive version.
  # Recheck LiteLLM's declared constraint on upgrade; the observability guard covers callback imports.
  "pydantic-settings==2.16.2",
  "html2text==2025.4.15",
  # pr_agent/telemetry imports these directly; already resolved transitively via
  # langfuse and litellm, pinned here to lock the version the code is tested against.
  "opentelemetry-api==1.45.1",
  "opentelemetry-sdk==1.45.1",
  "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.45.1",
  # Prometheus scrape endpoint for [otel] command telemetry (native /metrics on
  # the webhook apps). Multiprocess-capable; see pr_agent/telemetry/prometheus.py.
  "prometheus-client==0.26.0",
]

[project.urls]
"Homepage" = "https://github.com/the-pr-agent/pr-agent"
"Documentation" = "https://docs.pr-agent.ai/"
"Repository" = "https://github.com/the-pr-agent/pr-agent"
"Issues" = "https://github.com/the-pr-agent/pr-agent/issues"

[tool.setuptools]
include-package-data = true

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
pr_agent = ["py.typed"]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["."]
include = [
  "pr_agent*",
] # include pr_agent and any sub-packages it finds under it.

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Git/provider integrations are optional so a plain package install does not pull every SDK.
github = ["PyGithub>=2.10,<3"]
gitlab = ["python-gitlab==8.6.0"]
bitbucket = ["atlassian-python-api==5.0.5"]
azure = [
  "azure-devops==7.1.0b4",
  "azure-identity==1.27.0",
  "msrest==0.7.1",
]
codecommit = ["boto3==1.43.123"]
gitea = ["giteapy==1.0.8"]
google = [
  "google-cloud-aiplatform==2.7.0",
  # google-cloud-aiplatform==1.154.0 requires storage <4,>=1.32.0 on py<3.13 and <4,>=3.10.0 on py>=3.13.
  # Pin per-Python so existing installs are unchanged and py3.13 resolves. See #2480.
  "google-cloud-storage==2.10.0; python_version < '3.13'",
  "google-cloud-storage==3.12.0; python_version >= '3.13'",
  # Keep protobuf explicit to lock the transitive version resolved with the gRPC dependency stack.
  # Revalidate compatibility when updating grpcio-status or related Google/gRPC dependencies.
  "protobuf==6.33.6",
]
mosaico = ["a2a-sdk[http-server]==1.3.0"]
# Preserve the dependency set that the published Docker images shipped before provider SDKs became optional.
all = ["pr-agent[github,gitlab,bitbucket,azure,codecommit,gitea,google,mosaico]"]
# AWS Lambda deployment (docker/Dockerfile.lambda).
# Keep mangum >=0.21.0 for Python 3.14: older releases call
# asyncio.get_event_loop() with no fallback, which raises RuntimeError
# when no loop is set. Skip 0.20.0, whose 3.14 support was reverted
# upstream; 0.22.0 is end-to-end tested against a real Lambda runtime.
lambda = ["mangum==0.22.0"]
# OTLP/gRPC transport for pr-agent telemetry (OTEL.OTLP_PROTOCOL = "grpc").
# The default OTLP/HTTP transport needs no extra: its exporter is a base dependency.
otel-grpc = ["opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc==1.45.1"]

name: agent-browser
description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
readme_content:
# agent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell.

agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) ``` - **Homebrew:** `brew install agent-browser`, then `agent-browser install`. - **Linux:** `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries. - **No install:** `npx agent-browser open example.com`. Project installs, building from source, `upgrade`, and `doctor` are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-browser open example.com agent-browser snapshot -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-browser click @e1 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-browser get url # check the result agent-browser close ``` The snapshot for `example.com`: ``` - link "Learn more" [ref=e1] ``` - Refs describe the page at the time of the snapshot. After navigation or a DOM change, take a new snapshot before using refs again. - CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators also work, for example `agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"`. See [Selectors](https://agent-browser.dev/selectors). - A click fails, instead of reporting success, when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element such as a consent banner. Dismiss the covering element, take a new snapshot, and retry. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/quick-start). ## How it works The CLI sends each command to a background daemon that starts on the first command and controls the browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Each `--session` gets its own daemon and browser. By default, the daemon closes a headless browser and exits after one hour without commands, saving state first when [session persistence](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions) is configured. Chrome for Testing is the default browser. You can also attach to a running Chrome with `--cdp` or `--auto-connect` ([CDP mode](https://agent-browser.dev/cdp-mode)), select the [Lightpanda](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/lightpanda) or [Obscura](https://agent-browser.dev/engines/obscura) engine with `--engine`, drive Mobile Safari in the [iOS Simulator](https://agent-browser.dev/ios), or use a cloud browser provider such as [Browserbase](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserbase), [Browserless](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browserless), [Browser Use](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/browser-use), [Kernel](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/kernel), or [AgentCore](https://agent-browser.dev/providers/agentcore). ## For AI agents The CLI ships skills that match its version: ```bash agent-browser skills get core # the core loop, refs, waiting, and common workflows agent-browser skills get core --ref commands # one reference, such as the full command list agent-browser skills get core --full # adds the full command reference and templates agent-browser skills list # specialized skills: electron, slack, dogfood, and more ``` Install the discovery skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-browser): ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser ``` The installed skill is a thin stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the installed CLI. Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-browser` for browser automation. Before the first use, run `agent-browser skills get core` and follow it. ``` For MCP clients, `agent-browser mcp` starts an MCP server over stdio. See [MCP server](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#mcp-server). ## Commands Run `agent-browser --help` for the full list, or `agent-browser --help` for one command. | Group | Commands | Docs | |---|---|---| | Navigate and read | `open`, `back`, `forward`, `reload`, `read`, `snapshot`, `get`, `is` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Snapshots](https://agent-browser.dev/snapshots) | | Interact | `click`, `dblclick`, `fill`, `type`, `press`, `keyboard`, `hover`, `focus`, `select`, `check`, `uncheck`, `scroll`, `drag`, `upload`, `mouse`, `find` | [Core](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#core), [Find elements](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#find-elements) | | Wait | `wait` | [Wait](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#wait) | | Capture | `screenshot`, `pdf`, `record`, `download`, `diff` | [Recording](https://agent-browser.dev/recording), [Diffing](https://agent-browser.dev/diffing), [Files](https://agent-browser.dev/files) | | Page and network state | `cookies`, `storage`, `network`, `set`, `clipboard`, `eval`, `pushstate` | [Network](https://agent-browser.dev/network), [Settings](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#settings) | | Tabs, frames, and dialogs | `tab`, `frame`, `dialog` | [Tabs and frames](https://agent-browser.dev/commands#tabs-frames) | | Debug and performance | `console`, `errors`, `highlight`, `inspect`, `trace`, `profiler`, `vitals`, `react`, `a11y` | [Debugging](https://agent-browser.dev/debugging), [Profiler](https://agent-browser.dev/profiler), [React](https://agent-browser.dev/react) | | Sessions and auth | `session`, `state`, `auth`, `profiles`, `confirm`, `deny` | [Sessions](https://agent-browser.dev/sessions), [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security) | | Agents and integrations | `skills`, `mcp`, `webmcp`, `flow`, `chat`, `batch`, `plugin` | [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/skills), [WebMCP](https://agent-browser.dev/webmcp), [Plugins](https://agent-browser.dev/plugins) | | Observe | `stream`, `dashboard` | [Streaming](https://agent-browser.dev/streaming), [Dashboard](https://agent-browser.dev/dashboard) | | Setup | `install`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `connect`, `close` | [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/installation) | Flags, environment variables, and `agent-browser.json` are documented in [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration). ## Platforms Native binaries ship for macOS (ARM64, x64), Linux (ARM64, x64, glibc and musl), and Windows (x64). The npm package picks the right binary for the host. ## Development Building from source requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust: ```bash pnpm install pnpm build:source # builds the dashboard and the native CLI pnpm link --global agent-browser install ``` Run the Rust checks from `cli/`: ```bash cargo fmt -- --check cargo clippy cargo test cargo test e2e -- --ignored --test-threads=1 # launches real headless Chrome ``` [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) lists the files to update with each change, the docs checks, and the release process. ## Documentation - [agent-browser.dev](https://agent-browser.dev): introduction, guides, and reference - [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/commands) and [Configuration](https://agent-browser.dev/configuration) - [Security](https://agent-browser.dev/security): the auth vault, domain allowlists, action policies, and content boundaries - [Next.js and Vercel](https://agent-browser.dev/next) and [eve](https://agent-browser.dev/eve): running agent-browser in Vercel Sandbox and eve agents - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## License Apache-2.0

# Features - All of the eyecandy: gradient borders, many types of blur, animations, glow, shadows and much more - A lot of customization - 100% independent, no wlroots, no libweston, no kwin, no mutter. - Custom bezier and spring curves for the best animations - Powerful plugin support - Built-in plugin manager - Tearing support for better gaming performance - Easily expandable and readable codebase - Fast and active development - Not afraid to provide bleeding-edge features - Config reloaded instantly upon saving - Global keybinds passed to your apps of choice - Tiling/pseudotiling/floating/fullscreen windows - Special workspaces (scratchpads) - Window groups (tabbed mode) - Powerful window/monitor/layer rules - Socket-based IPC - Native IME and Input Panels Support - Fully dynamic workspaces - Extensive layout support - Dwindle - Scrolling - Master - Monocle - Custom layout with Lua - Custom layouts with plugins - Per Workspace Layouts - and much more...

readme_content:
# Marketing Skills for AI Agents

A collection of AI agent skills focused on marketing tasks. Built for technical marketers and founders who want AI coding agents to help with conversion optimization, copywriting, SEO, analytics, and growth engineering. Works with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, and any agent that supports the [Agent Skills spec](https://agentskills.io).

Built by [Corey Haines](https://corey.co?ref=marketingskills). Need hands-on help? Check out [Conversion Factory](https://conversionfactory.co?ref=marketingskills) — Corey's agency for conversion optimization, landing pages, and growth strategy. Want to learn more about marketing? Subscribe to [Swipe Files](https://swipefiles.com?ref=marketingskills). Want to get dangerously good at using AI for marketing? Check out [AI Marketing Training](https://conversionfactory.co/offers/ai-marketing-training?ref=marketingskills). Want an autonomous AI agent that uses these skills to be your CMO? Try [Magister](https://magistermarketing.com?ref=marketingskills).

New to the terminal and coding agents? Check out the companion guide [Coding for Marketers](https://codingformarketers.com?ref=marketingskills).

Want your agent to read your marketing accounts? Follow the [guided tool connection workflow](tools/SETUP.md) for scoped credentials and a first read-only result.

**Contributions welcome!** Found a way to improve a skill or have a new one to add? [Open a PR](#contributing).

Run into a problem or have a question? [Open an issue](https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills/issues) — we're happy to help.

## Partners

The library is free and MIT-licensed. [Verified Partners](tools/REGISTRY.md#verified-partners) fund the work — vetted, disclosed tool integrations, listed alongside the neutral options and never influencing what the core skills recommend. The full rules and boundaries are in [tools/PARTNERS.md](tools/PARTNERS.md). [Become a partner →](https://marketing-skills.com/sponsorship)

<!-- PARTNERS:START -->
> ◆ **[Converly](https://converly.io)** — *Conversion tracking / attribution.* Server-side conversion tracking that fires when someone submits a form, books a meeting, or starts a chat — passing click IDs and identifiers for Enhanced Conversions (Google) and stronger match quality (Meta), across about 100 tools. CLI + MCP so your agent sets it up in minutes. → [Integration guide](tools/integrations/converly.md)

> ◆ **[Ploy](https://ploy.ai)** — *AI website & growth platform.* AI marketing platform built around a hosted website builder — an in-app agent that builds and publishes pages, PloyDB for pages at scale, routing to add pages to an existing site, built-in analytics and visitor identification, and a CLI for coding agents. → [Integration guide](tools/integrations/ploy.md)

> ◆ **[AIsa](https://aisa.one)** — *SEO, search & social data.* One AIsa key, pay as you go, instead of a subscription to every data platform. Agents get SEO, search, social, and market data from Similarweb, Semrush, Ahrefs, DataForSEO, Tavily, Reddit, X, and more through REST or MCP, and pay only for the calls they make. → [Integration guide](tools/integrations/aisa.md)

> ◆ **[Omnia](https://www.useomnia.com)** — *AI search visibility (AEO).* Omnia tracks how AI engines answer your customers' questions every day: visibility, citations, Share of Voice and sentiment for your brand and competitors. Connect the Omnia MCP to Claude and these skills run on real AI answers data instead of guesses. Or let your Omnia Agent turn it into prioritized work that you review and approve. → [Integration guide](tools/integrations/omnia.md)
<!-- PARTNERS:END -->

<!-- The Partners block above is generated from partners.json — run `node scripts/sync-partners.mjs` after editing it. -->

## What are Skills?

Skills are markdown files that give AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows for specific tasks. When you add these to your project, your agent can recognize when you're working on a marketing task and apply the right frameworks and best practices.

## How Skills Work Together

Skills reference each other and build on shared context. The `product-marketing` skill is the foundation — every other skill checks it first to understand your product, audience, and positioning before doing anything.

description: Open-source AI coworkers that each get a computer of their own: a browser, files and tools, with every action decided before it happens and recorded after. Bring any AG-UI agent.
readme_content:
# OpenBot ### AI coworkers. Ready for the enterprise. A modular, self-hostable workspace for AI coworkers.
Choose your models. Bring your agents. Own your infrastructure. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) [Kubernetes](#deploy-on-kubernetes) [**OpenBot for Business · Get early access →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Docs**](docs/README.md) From [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), creators of [AG-UI](https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui).
## Getting started ### On your laptop The easiest way to get started is with the fully self-contained app that runs on your laptop, combining the OpenBot frontend and Docker-based backend in one application. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Run from source](#run-from-source) ### For your team **OpenBot for Business** brings your agents into one workspace with company sign-in, tool permissions, approvals, and audit. Deploy on your infrastructure or work with our engineers on hosting and customization. [**Get early access to OpenBot for Business →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Talk to an engineer**](https://open.bot/business) · [**Kubernetes setup**](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ### Web, mobile, and chat [Web](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=web&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) ## See it in action https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/535ef7ee-1631-4a69-b839-564c56cf90b4 Watch a Bot use its browser and tools, review interactive results, and take over when it needs you. Teach it repeatable tasks through feedback and demonstrations. ## Your workspace. Your stack.
- **Choose your models.** Use OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or open models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted by a provider or on your own infrastructure. Keep your provider relationships and change models as your needs change. - **Bring your agents.** Run built-in Bots in the OpenBot server, or connect your existing agents through AG-UI from any agent execution platform. LangChain, Claude Agent SDK, Google ADK, Mastra, CrewAI, AWS Strands, and more can work in the same workspace. - **Make it yours.** Use the MIT-licensed template as-is, white-label it, or customize it deeply. AG-UI connects agents, MCP connects tools, and the frontends and backend can evolve independently. - **Govern work across your team.** Company sign-in, roles, tool permissions, approvals, and audit apply across the workspace. Your agents use OpenBot's tools and computers under the same policies. - **Get help deploying it.** CopilotKit's engineers can work with your team to deploy OpenBot, connect your systems, and automate parts of specific jobs. [Connect your agent](#bring-your-own-agent) · [Configure models and tools](docs/configuration.md) · [Explore OpenBot for Business](https://open.bot/business) ## Architecture OpenBot has three parts. On your laptop, setup runs the backend and Intelligence for you. For a team, the Helm chart deploys both on Kubernetes in your own infrastructure. | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **OpenBot frontends** | Mac, Windows, web, iOS, Android, Slack, and Teams connect people to the same workspace. Conversations, interactive results, computer view, and approvals adapt to each surface. [Choose a frontend](#getting-started). | | **OpenBot backend** | Runs the workspace API and built-in Bots, connects external agents and tools, manages Bot computers, and enforces identity, permissions, action policies, and audit. Deploys on Kubernetes with PostgreSQL and persistent storage. | | **CopilotKit Intelligence** | Durable conversations, memory, Automatic Learning, and enterprise governance services. Separately licensed; runs on Kubernetes alongside OpenBot. | OpenBot enforces sign-in, tool permissions, action policies, and audit at its API, alongside Intelligence's platform services. Built-in Bots run in the OpenBot server; your own agents can run alongside OpenBot or on any agent execution platform. Both use AG-UI and can share the same workspace. Computer execution is pluggable: use the default Kubernetes setup or connect a compatible external computer provider. [Architecture details](docs/architecture.md) · [Services and ports](#services-and-ports) · [Kubernetes deployment](charts/openbot/README.md) ## Open source, local operation, and licensing **The OpenBot application template is open source under the [MIT license](LICENSE).** You can fork, modify, and white-label it. It uses **CopilotKit Intelligence**, which is separately licensed and can run entirely on your own machine or infrastructure. | Where you run it | CopilotKit Intelligence license | | --- | --- | | **Your laptop, for personal use and experimentation** | Requires a free local Intelligence license. Desktop setup handles this for you. | | **Kubernetes evaluation** | Requires a free Intelligence trial license. [Request a trial](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access). | | **Kubernetes / production** | Requires a production Intelligence license beyond evaluation. OpenBot for Business includes Intelligence for use with OpenBot. [Plans and pricing](https://open.bot/pricing). | **Fully local is an option.** Run OpenBot, Intelligence, and a compatible model locally. A cloud model or connected online app still sends requests to that service. Initial downloads, account sign-in, and local license renewal need internet access. --- ## Deploy on Kubernetes Deploy OpenBot and CopilotKit Intelligence together on **AWS EKS, Azure AKS, Google GKE, or your own Kubernetes cluster**. The chart installs Intelligence by default; no separate hosted project is required. For a first evaluation, you need a cluster with **amd64 nodes**, a **default StorageClass**, `kubectl`, Helm, a **trial or production license**, and a model key. The commands below use an OpenAI key. For Anthropic, a model router, cluster sizing, or an existing Intelligence deployment, use the [full Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md). > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Give it this README and [the Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md). The guide covers cloud-specific values, storage, secrets, sign-in, networking, upgrades, and troubleshooting. Use the evaluation below only through a local port-forward; configure sign-in and TLS before sharing a deployment. 1. **Get the source.** Skip this if you already have a checkout. ```sh git clone https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot.git cd OpenBot ``` 2. **Create `openbot-secrets.yaml` locally.** Replace the placeholders with your license and model key. Keep this file out of source control. ```yaml secrets: licenseToken: "" modelApiKey: "" ``` 3. **Install.** ```sh helm dependency build charts/openbot helm install openbot charts/openbot \ --namespace openbot --create-namespace \ --values charts/openbot/ci/vanilla-values.yaml \ --values openbot-secrets.yaml \ --timeout 15m ``` 4. **Open your evaluation.** ```sh kubectl -n openbot get pods,jobs kubectl -n openbot port-forward svc/openbot-server 3001:3001 ``` Open . This configuration is single-user: anyone who can reach it is an administrator. Keep the port-forward local. The chart creates the runtime credentials, installs the databases, bootstraps Intelligence, and sets up the Learning container and scheduled jobs. Automatic Learning uses your model key too. For a team deployment, follow the [Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md) to configure authentication, TLS, your database, secrets, persistent storage, and network policies. For a single-container alternative, see [Deploy it](#deploy-it). ## Run from source Use the template to customize the workspace, branding, Bots, and skills. The source setup below uses managed Intelligence by default; [local Intelligence](#intelligence-on-your-own-machine) is also available. ```sh git clone https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot.git cd OpenBot ``` ### Requirements To run the open-source template locally, you’ll need the following. - Docker, for PostgreSQL and the shipped Bots. - [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4+, for the app, the API server and the tests (some tests fail on 1.3). - A CopilotKit Intelligence project and license. A free plan is available, and Intelligence can be self-hosted. - A model key. The proof-of-concept Bot uses OpenAI; the LangGraph Bot can use OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google. ### Quick start The example configuration sets `OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true`, so you can try the app as a local administrator. Configure [sign-in](#sign-in) before giving anyone else access. On a Mac, the free Developer plan also covers

name: codex
description: Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal
readme_content:
Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer.


If you want Codex in your code editor (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf), install in your IDE.
If you want the desktop app experience, run codex app or visit the Codex App page.
If you are looking for the cloud-based agent from OpenAI, Codex Web, go to chatgpt.com/codex.

--- ## Quickstart ### Installing and running Codex CLI Run the following on Mac or Linux to install Codex CLI: ```shell curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh ``` Run the following on Windows to install Codex CLI: ```shell powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex" ``` The standalone installers download from `https://releases.openai.com/codex` by default and fall back to GitHub Releases if a metadata or asset download is unavailable. To force GitHub Releases, set `CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM` to `false` (`0` and `no` are also accepted): ```shell curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM=false sh ``` ```powershell $env:CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM='false'; irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex ``` Codex CLI can also be installed via the following package managers: ```shell # Install using npm npm install -g @openai/codex ``` ```shell # Install using Homebrew brew install --cask codex ``` Then simply run `codex` to get started.
You can also go to the latest GitHub Release and download the appropriate binary for your platform. Each GitHub Release contains many executables, but in practice, you likely want one of these: - macOS - Apple Silicon/arm64: `codex-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` - x86_64 (older Mac hardware): `codex-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` - Linux - x86_64: `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` - arm64: `codex-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` Each archive contains a single entry with the platform baked into the name (e.g., `codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`), so you likely want to rename it to `codex` after extracting it.
### Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan Run `codex` and select **Sign in with ChatGPT**. We recommend signing into your ChatGPT account to use Codex as part of your Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plan. [Learn more about what's included in your ChatGPT plan](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11369540-codex-in-chatgpt). You can also use Codex with an API key, but this requires [additional setup](https://developers.openai.com/codex/auth#sign-in-with-an-api-key). ## Docs - [**Codex Documentation**](https://developers.openai.com/codex) - [**Contributing**](./docs/contributing.md) - [**Installing & building**](./docs/install.md) - [**Open source fund**](./docs/open-source-fund.md) This repository is licensed under the [Apache-2.0 License](LICENSE).

[License](#license) | --- ### [`motion-showreel`](./skills/motion-showreel) ![Motion Showreel Skill](./dist/imgs/covers/motion-showreel.webp) **Category:** Motion Graphics / Code Video **Best for:** showreels, product films, UI motion, kinetic typography, logo/title sequences, generative loops, retrospectives and narrated explainers. Short pieces typically run 5–60 s; chapter-based films support up to 20 minutes. `motion-showreel` delivers MP4 plus editable source. It confirms the topic, duration, orientation, independent music/SFX sources and narration mode, then writes a brief and confirms style frames. Deterministic `render(t)` pages are captured frame by frame on a shared audio/picture timeline. Narration follows a user-supplied script or recording; pictures follow actual speech timings. Long films use persistent chapter caches and technical acceptance. Highlights: - **Deterministic `render(t)` pipeline**: stills, contact sheets, three-direction boards, proxies and masters all come from the same page. Motion blur, supersampling and film grain are render flags. - **One timeline for picture and sound**: cuts, hits and SFX share the same numbers. Music can be synthesized (a zero-dependency built-in synth, or Tone.js with a sampled piano), or cut to the user's own track with beat and drop detection. - **A 43-style library as a starting point**: swiss-editorial, ink-wash, risograph, synthwave, soft 3D, cinematic title, pixel game, comic panels, guochao patterns, painterly strokes, whiteboard explainers, concept morphs, illuminated manuscripts and more. Each style defines its look, motion, camera grammar and sound palette, and can be adapted, mixed or replaced with your own. - **A sound direction, not a default song**: the brief sets a sound benchmark, groove, harmony, palette and dramatic arc, plus a list of audio defaults to avoid. - **Two checkpoints**: confirm requirements, then style frames (three distinct directions when unspecified), followed by autonomous production. Creative freedom remains available. - **Narration and long films**: Gemini/MiniMax TTS reads only user-supplied scripts; recordings use real timestamps. Music and SFX have independent sources, yield to speech, and chapter builds support up to 20 minutes. - **Technical acceptance kept separate from taste**: size, fps, duration, frame count, black frames, loudness, true peak, loop seam and determinism must all PASS. Review notes go to the user, who makes the final call.

name: sellbird
description: Sellbird (formerly Harvey): the open-source outreach platform that runs on your Claude or ChatGPT plan. Finds companies and decision makers, verifies emails, writes personal cold email, sends it and handles the replies.
readme_content:
The open-source outreach platform that runs on your Claude or ChatGPT plan.

Sellbird finds companies that need what you sell, finds the person who decides, checks their email address, writes each one a personal cold email, sends it and handles the replies. It runs on your own machine, and by default nothing goes out until you approve it.

> **[Harvey is now Sellbird.](https://sellbird.ai/harvey/)** Same project, same history, new name. Already running Harvey? Your setup carries over: see [Upgrading from Harvey](#upgrading-from-harvey). **Prefer not to run it yourself? [sellbird.ai](https://sellbird.ai) is the hosted version, with sending domains, inboxes and warmup set up for you. It's in early access.** ![Sellbird's dashboard: the Today screen, a conversation that needs you, approving a drafted reply in the Outbox, the signals to confirm, searching contacts, then dark mode](docs/dashboard.gif) The demo data is invented: "Bookwell" selling online booking to roofers, dental practices and HVAC shops, on `.test` domains. ## What it does Sellbird is a pipeline you can run end to end, or stop at any step. | | What happens | More | |---|---|---| | **Find companies** | Searches for businesses that match your customer: free on OpenStreetMap, or on a paid source you pick. Every paid search shows its cost before it runs. | [Discovery](docs/signals-and-pipeline.md#1-discover--who-exists) | | **Learn why they'd buy** | Reads each company's own website for the buying signals you confirmed, like no online booking, ads running or a role they're hiring for. No model calls, no cost. | [Signals](docs/signals-and-pipeline.md) | | **Find who decides** | Finds the owner or manager named on the company's own pages, two people per company at most. | [Enrich](docs/signals-and-pipeline.md#3-enrich--who-decides) | | **Check the address** | Learns the company's email pattern and verifies one address. Every address is marked verified, risky, guess or invalid, and only deliverable ones are ever sent to. | [Verify](docs/signals-and-pipeline.md#4-verify--can-you-reach-them) | | **Write and send** | Writes a short sequence for each person from what it found, then sends from your Gmail, Microsoft 365 or SMTP mailbox inside your daily limit and their office hours. | [Sending](docs/approval-and-sending.md) | | **Handle replies** | Reads every reply, drafts an answer, sets auto-replies aside, honours opt-outs at once, and hands you anything it shouldn't answer alone. | [Dashboard](docs/dashboard.md) | Only want the list? Stop after verifying and run `sellbird export` for a sequencer-ready CSV of everything it found. ``` $ sellbird run ============================================================ Sellbird is online. ============================================================ Checking pipeline state... Decision: write_campaign (3 new prospects with no drafts) handler → Elena Park, Harbor Dental Studio interested, answer drafted handler → Priya Nair, Highline Roofing objection, answer drafted writer → 2-email sequence: Phoenix HVAC hiring a dispatcher outbox → 5 emails waiting for your approval Cycle complete. Sleeping for 15 minutes. ``` ## No model API bill Sellbird thinks through the Claude Code CLI on your Claude Pro or Max plan, or through Codex on a ChatGPT plan. There's no API key and no per-token billing, and Sellbird throttles itself to leave room for your own work. | | | |---|---| | Claude Pro or Max, or a ChatGPT plan with Codex | the subscription you already have | | Finding businesses | **$0** on the default source, or about $0.37 per 1,000 on the cheapest paid one | | Reading their websites | **$0**: three HTTP requests each, no model call | | Writing and sending | your subscription and a mailbox (about $7 a month for Google Workspace) | | Prospecting tools | **None.** No Apollo, ZoomInfo, Clearbit or Clay. | How the loop, the budget and the isolation work: [How Sellbird works](docs/how-it-works.md). ## Quick start You need: - **Python 3.11 or newer.** macOS ships 3.9, so run `brew install python@3.13` first if `python3 --version` says so. - **Claude Pro or Max** with the CLI signed in (`claude login`), or a **ChatGPT plan with the Codex CLI** ([Codex setup](docs/codex.md)). - **A mailbox to send from**, ideally Google Workspace on a separate sending domain. [Microsoft 365](docs/microsoft365.md) and SMTP work too. - **Warmup on that mailbox.** We recommend [TrulyInbox](https://trulyinbox.com/?via=sellbird): it warms a new mailbox before cold email and keeps it out of spam after, and Sellbird reads its inbox rate to tell you when you're ready. ### Let Claude set it up ```bash git clone https://github.com/ethanplusai/sellbird.git cd sellbird claude ``` Then say **"set up Sellbird for me"**. The repo's `CLAUDE.md` turns Claude Code into the setup guide: it checks where you are, installs what's missing, asks what it needs and trains Sellbird on your product. ### Or do it yourself ```bash # 1. Install. Use python3.13, not python3: on macOS bare python3 is 3.9. python3.13 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e . # 2. Add credentials. Every variable is documented inline. cp .env.example .env && $EDITOR .env # 3. Learn your product from your website (writes sellbird.local.yaml). sellbird train https://your-company.com # 4. Confirm what makes a good prospect. sellbird signals --confirm free # 5. Find businesses. The default source is free and needs no account. sellbird discover # 6. Open the dashboard and start the loop. sellbird dashboard # prints a private link to http://127.0.0.1:5555 sellbird run ``` On Linux you can also [run it with Docker](docs/docker.md). ## Nothing sends without you Every outgoing email waits in the Outbox for your approval until you turn on autopilot yourself. Before anything leaves, a pre-send check with no model involved rejects unfilled merge tags, banned phrases, overlong emails, extra links and undeliverable addresses. Autopilot still holds back any email that links to a domain that isn't yours or quotes Sellbird's own instructions. `sellbird sending pause` stops everything at once. Details: [Approval and sending](docs/approval-and-sending.md) and [Legal and deliverability](docs/deliverability.md). ## Upgrading from Harvey Harvey was renamed Sellbird in 0.4.0. Your configuration, data and dashboard sign-in carry over: ```bash git pull pip install -e . # once, to get the new `sellbird` command sellbird dashboard ``` - On first run Sellbird renames `harvey.local.yaml` to `sellbird.local.yaml` and `data/harvey.db` (and its log) to `data/sellbird.*`. It never overwrites a file that already exists under the new name, and waits if a Harvey process is still running from the folder. Stop that first. - `HARVEY_*` environment variables still work when the `SELLBIRD_*` one isn't set; rename them when convenient. - The `harvey` command and `python -m harvey` still work for now and say they moved. They will be removed in a later release. - If you edited the tracked `harvey.yaml` directly, `git pull` stops with "your local changes would be overwritten". Run `git stash`, `git pull`, then `git stash pop`. Git carries your edits into `sellbird.yaml`. If it reports a conflict there, keep your lines, delete the conflict markers, and run `git stash drop`. Better still, put your settings in `sellbird.local.yaml`, which git never touches. - Docker: the service is now `sellbird`. Run `docker compose down`, `git pull`, `docker compose build`, then `docker compose up -d`. `HARVEY_UID`/`HARVEY_GID` are still read. Links to `github.com/ethanplusai/harvey` keep working: GitHub redirects them here. ## Where your files live Your config, knowledge and data live in one home folder. Which one, first match wins: 1. `SELLBIRD_HOME`, if you set it (the Docker image sets it to `/app`). 2. A checkout: the checkout folder itself, as before. 3. Otherwise, for an installed package (`pip` or `pipx`), your user data folder: | | Home folder | |---|---| | macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/sellbird` | | Windows | `%APPDATA%\sellbird` | | Linux | `~/.local/share/sellbird` (or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/sellbird`) | Inside it are `sellbird.yaml` (and `sellbird.local.yaml` once you train), `.env`, `prompts/` and `skills/`, all yours to edit. An installed package copies the defaults in on first run and never overwrites them, so your edits survive upgrades. `data/` holds the database, the logs and the dashboard token. ## Documentation | Guide | What's in it | |---|---| | [How Sellbird works](docs/how-it-works.md) | The heartbeat loop, the subscription budget, project structure and the ideas behind it | | [Signals and the prospecting pipeline](docs/signals-and-pipeline.md) | The 29 signals, cohorts, and the discover, profile, enrich and verify stages | | [Skills and sub-agents](docs/skills-and-agents.md) | The editable sales playbooks and which agent uses which | | [Approval and sending](docs/approval-and-sending.md) | The Outbox, autopilot, office hours and email signatures | | [The dashboard and the data](docs/dashboard.md) | Every screen, how sign-in works, and how the data is stored | | [Configuration and commands](docs/configuration.md) | `.env`, `sellbird.yaml` and every command | | [Extensions](docs/extensions.md) | Adding routes, heartbeat steps and commands from a separate package | | [Using a ChatGPT plan (Codex)](docs/codex.md) | Running on Codex instead of Claude | | [Legal and deliverability](docs/deliverability.md) | The rules you're sending under, and warmup | | [Microsoft 365](docs/microsoft365.md) · [Precleared](docs/precleared.md) | Provider setup guides | | [Docker](docs/docker.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) · [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Running, fixing and what's next | ## Contributing Pull requests are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first: it covers keeping real contact data out of the repo, test email, and signing off your commits. Found a security problem? Follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead of opening an issue. See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for what changed in each release. ## License Sellbird is licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0](LICENSE). Harvey releases up to 0.3.x were released under MIT, and that code keeps its MIT notice in [NOTICE](NOTICE). TrulyInbox links in this project are affiliate links: the maintainer may earn a commission, at no extra cost to you.

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "sellbird"
version = "0.4.0"
description = "Sellbird: the open-source outreach platform. Finds companies and the people who decide, writes personal cold email, sends it and handles replies."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
keywords = ["sales", "outreach", "ai-agent", "cold-email", "prospecting", "autonomous-agent", "claude"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Office/Business",
]
# Keep in sync with requirements.txt (used by Docker builds).
dependencies = [
    "pyyaml>=6.0.1,<7",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.1,<2",
    "httpx>=0.27.0,<1",
    "playwright>=1.40,<2",
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.12.3,<5",
    "dnspython>=2.4.2,<3",
    "aiosmtplib>=5.1.3,<6",
    "aiosqlite>=0.19,<1",
    "keyring>=25,<26",
    # The menu-bar app (sellbird tray): macOS and Windows only.
    'pystray>=0.19.5,<0.20; sys_platform == "darwin" or sys_platform == "win32"',
    'Pillow>=10,<12; sys_platform == "darwin" or sys_platform == "win32"',
    "pydantic>=2.5,<3",
    "pytz>=2024.1",
    "fastapi>=0.115,<1",
    "uvicorn>=0.34,<1",
    "mcp>=2.3,<3",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0,<9",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23,<1",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/ethanplusai/sellbird"
Issues = "https://github.com/ethanplusai/sellbird/issues"
Changelog = "https://github.com/ethanplusai/sellbird/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"

[project.scripts]
sellbird = "sellbird.cli:main"
# The old name, kept for a while so existing installs keep working (harvey/).
harvey = "harvey.cli:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["sellbird*", "harvey*"]

# The editable defaults an installed app seeds its home folder from
# (sellbird/home.py). They land in <prefix>/share/sellbird.
[tool.setuptools]
data-files = {"share/sellbird" = ["sellbird.yaml", ".env.example"], "share/sellbird/prompts" = ["prompts/*.md"], "share/sellbird/skills" = ["skills/*.md"]}

# The dashboard's HTML/CSS/JS are real files served from disk, and its fonts
# are vendored so a local tool renders correctly with the network off.
[tool.setuptools.package-data]
sellbird = ["web/*", "web/fonts/*"]

name: skills
description: The open agent skills tool - npx skills
readme_content:
# skills The CLI for the open agent skills ecosystem. Agent skills are reusable instructions that teach coding agents how to perform tasks, from reviewing code to working with a library. Discover skills at [skills.sh](https://skills.sh). Supports **OpenCode**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **Cursor**, and [75 more](docs/agents.md).

## Install a Skill Requires Node.js 22.20 or later. Run this from your project: ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills ``` Choose the skills and coding agents to install to. Skills are installed to the current project by default; add `-g` to make them available across projects. ```bash # Choose one skill and agent npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines -a claude-code # Browse available skills npx skills find ``` See the [installation reference](docs/commands.md#skills-add) for source formats, private repositories, and all options. ## Other Commands | Command | Description | | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | | `npx skills find [query]` | Search for skills | | `npx skills list` | List installed skills | | `npx skills use @` | Use one skill without installing | | `npx skills check` | Check for available updates | | `npx skills update [skills...]` | Update installed skills | | `npx skills remove [skills...]` | Remove installed skills | | `npx skills init [name]` | Create a skill template | Read the [CLI reference](docs/commands.md) or run `npx skills --help` for examples and options. Experimental commands are listed [below](#experimental-features). ## Use a Skill Without Installing Generate a prompt for a skill, or launch a supported coding agent with it: ```bash npx skills use vercel-labs/agent-skills@web-design-guidelines --agent claude-code ``` Omit `--agent` to print the prompt instead. See [`skills use`](docs/commands.md#skills-use). ## Experimental Features
Commands prefixed with experimental_ are previews. Their names, options, and behavior may change or be removed in any release without notice. | Command | Description | | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | | `npx skills experimental_sync` | Sync skills shipped by npm dependencies into your project | | `npx skills experimental_install` | Restore project skills recorded in `skills-lock.json` | Some npm packages bundle instructions for your agent alongside their code. Sync links them into your project so they update with the dependency, and also installs skill packs declared in `package.json`: ```bash npm install -D skills agent-browser npx skills experimental_sync -y ``` See the [experimental commands reference](docs/commands.md#experimental-commands) for options, the `skills` field, and the [RFC](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/2323) behind it.
## Supported Agents The CLI detects installed agents and lets you choose where skills are installed. See [all supported agents, installation paths, and compatibility](docs/agents.md). ## Creating Skills ```bash npx skills init my-skill ``` Edit the generated `SKILL.md` with instructions for your agent. See [creating and sharing skills](docs/creating-skills.md) for the format and discovery rules. ## Documentation - [CLI reference](docs/commands.md): installation, command examples, and experimental features - [Supported agents](docs/agents.md): agent names, skill directories, and compatibility - [Creating skills](docs/creating-skills.md): frontmatter, repository layouts, and plugins - [Troubleshooting and configuration](docs/troubleshooting.md): common problems, environment variables, and telemetry - [Programmatic API](docs/api.md): install and manage skills from your own tools with `import { installSkills } from 'skills'` ## Telemetry The CLI collects anonymous usage data. Set `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` to disable telemetry and security-audit requests. See [what is collected](docs/troubleshooting.md#telemetry). ## Related Links - [Skills Directory](https://skills.sh) - [Agent Skills Specification](https://agentskills.io) - [Vercel Agent Skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) ## License This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

name: project-nomad
description: Project NOMAD is an offline-first knowledge and education server. Wikipedia, thousands of books, courses, maps, and optional local AI, all running on hardware you own with no internet required.
readme_content:
# Project NOMAD ### Knowledge That Never Goes Offline [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-projectnomad.us-blue)](https://www.projectnomad.us) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join%20Community-5865F2)](https://discord.com/invite/crosstalksolutions) [![Benchmark](https://img.shields.io/badge/Benchmark-Leaderboard-green)](https://benchmark.projectnomad.us)
--- Project NOMAD is a self-contained, offline-first knowledge and education server packed with critical tools, knowledge, and AI to keep you informed and empowered — anytime, anywhere. ## Installation & Quickstart Project NOMAD can be installed on any Debian-based operating system (we recommend Ubuntu 26.04 LTS; 24.04 LTS and Debian 12 are also supported). Installation is completely terminal-based, and all tools and resources are designed to be accessed through the browser, so there's no need for a desktop environment if you'd rather setup NOMAD as a "server" and access it through other clients. **Before you start:** NOMAD itself needs about **5 GB of disk and under 1 GB of RAM**. The offline content you add afterwards is what actually fills a drive, and the AI Assistant is what drives the memory requirement up. See [Device Requirements](#device-requirements) for both, and the [FAQ](https://www.projectnomad.us/docs/faq) for individual content sizes. *Note: sudo/root privileges are required to run the install script* ### Quick Install (Debian-based OS Only) ```bash sudo apt-get update && \ sudo apt-get install -y curl && \ curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Crosstalk-Solutions/project-nomad/refs/heads/main/install/install_nomad.sh \ -o install_nomad.sh && \ sudo bash install_nomad.sh ``` Project NOMAD is now installed on your device! Open a browser and navigate to `http://localhost:8080` (or `http://DEVICE_IP:8080`) to start exploring! For a complete step-by-step walkthrough (including Ubuntu installation), see the [Installation Guide](https://www.projectnomad.us/install). For Windows users, see the [WSL2 install guide](https://www.projectnomad.us/install/wsl2) — community-supported path covering native Docker and Docker Desktop install routes. ### Advanced Installation For more control over the installation process, copy and paste the [Docker Compose template](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Crosstalk-Solutions/project-nomad/refs/heads/main/install/management_compose.yaml) into a `docker-compose.yml` file and customize it to your liking (be sure to replace any placeholders with your actual values). Then, run `docker compose up -d` to start the Command Center and its dependencies. Note: this method is recommended for advanced users only, as it requires familiarity with Docker and manual configuration before starting. ## How It Works NOMAD is a management UI ("Command Center") and API that orchestrates a collection of containerized tools and resources via [Docker](https://www.docker.com/). It handles installation, configuration, and updates for everything — so you don't have to. **Built-in capabilities include:** - **AI Chat with Knowledge Base** — local AI chat powered by [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) or you can use OpenAI API compatible software such as LM Studio or llama.cpp, with document upload and semantic search (RAG via [Qdrant](https://qdrant.tech/)) - **Information Library** — offline Wikipedia, medical references, ebooks, and more via [Kiwix](https://kiwix.org/) - **Education Platform** — Khan Academy courses with progress tracking via [Kolibri](https://learningequality.org/kolibri/) - **Offline Maps** — downloadable regional maps via [ProtoMaps](https://protomaps.com) - **Data Tools** — encryption, encoding, and analysis via [CyberChef](https://gchq.github.io/CyberChef/) - **Notes** — local note-taking via [FlatNotes](https://github.com/dullage/flatnotes) - **System Benchmark** — hardware scoring with a [community leaderboard](https://benchmark.projectnomad.us) - **Supply Depot** — a one-click app catalog (PDF tools, file browser, e-book library, password manager, and more) plus the ability to run your own custom Docker containers - **Automatic Updates** — opt-in, hands-off updates for the core software, installed apps, and offline content, on a schedule you control - **Easy Setup Wizard** — guided first-time configuration with curated content collections NOMAD also includes built-in tools like a Wikipedia content selector, ZIM library manager, and content explorer. ## What's Included | Capability | Powered By | What You Get | |-----------|-----------|-------------| | Information Library | Kiwix | Offline Wikipedia, medical references, survival guides, ebooks | | AI Assistant | Ollama + Qdrant | Built-in chat with document upload and semantic search | | Education Platform | Kolibri | Khan Academy courses, progress tracking, multi-user support | | Offline Maps | ProtoMaps | Downloadable regional maps for offline viewing and search | | Data Tools | CyberChef | Encryption, encoding, hashing, and data analysis | | Notes | FlatNotes | Local note-taking with markdown support | | System Benchmark | Built-in | Hardware scoring, Builder Tags, and community leaderboard | | Supply Depot | Built-in | One-click app catalog + bring-your-own custom Docker containers | ## Device Requirements While many similar offline survival computers are designed to be run on bare-minimum, lightweight hardware, Project NOMAD is quite the opposite. To install and run the available AI tools, we highly encourage the use of a beefy, GPU-backed device to make the most of your install. At its core, however, NOMAD is still very lightweight. For a barebones installation of the management application itself, the following minimal specs are required: *Note: Project NOMAD is not sponsored by any hardware manufacturer and is designed to be as hardware-agnostic as possible. The hardware listed below is for example/comparison use only* #### Minimum Specs - Processor: 2 GHz dual-core processor or better - RAM: 4GB system memory (the whole stack without AI runs in under 1 GB) - Storage: At least 5 GB free disk space (plan for 10 GB to install comfortably) - OS: Debian-based (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS recommended) - Stable internet connection (required during install only) Adding the AI Assistant brings the install to roughly **25 GB**, because Ollama and a general-purpose model are both large, and a model needs about its download size in memory while it answers. That memory comes from VRAM if you have a discrete GPU and from system RAM if you do not, which is the single biggest reason the figures below are so much higher. To run LLMs and other included AI tools: #### Optimal Specs - Processor: AMD Ryzen 7 or Intel Core i7 or better - RAM: 32 GB system memory - Graphics: NVIDIA RTX 3060 or AMD equivalent or better (more VRAM = run larger models) - Storage: At least 250 GB free disk space (preferably on SSD) - OS: Debian-based (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS recommended) - Stable internet connection (required during install only) **For detailed build recommendations at three price points ($150–$1,000+), see the [Hardware Guide](https://www.projectnomad.us/hardware).** Again, Project NOMAD itself is quite lightweight — it's the tools and resources you choose to install with NOMAD that will determine the specs required for your unique deployment #### Running AI models on a different host By default, NOMAD's installer will attempt to setup Ollama on the host when the AI Assistant is installed. However, if you would like to run the AI model on a different host, you can go to the settings of the AI assistant and input a URL for either an ollama or OpenAI-compatible API server (such as LM Studio). Note that if you use Ollama on a different host, you must start the server with this option: `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`. Ollama is the preferred way to use the AI assistant, as it has features such as model download that OpenAI API does not support. So when using LM Studio, for example, you will have to use LM Studio to download models. You are responsible for the setup of Ollama/OpenAI server on the other host. ## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) For answers to common questions about Project NOMAD, please see our [FAQ](FAQ.md) page. ## About Internet Usage & Privacy Project NOMAD is designed for offline usage. An internet connection is only required during the initial installation (to download dependencies) and if you (the user) decide to download additional tools and resources at a later time. Otherwise, NOMAD does not require an internet connection and has ZERO built-in telemetry. To test internet connectivity, NOMAD first attempts to make a request to Cloudflare's utility endpoint, `https://1.1.1.1/cdn-cgi/trace`. If that endpoint is unreachable (for example, because your network blocks `1.1.1.1`), it falls back to other endpoints the application already contacts (the GitHub API and the Project NOMAD API) and considers the connection online if any of them respond. You can override the endpoint used for this check in two ways. The connectivity test URL can be configured from the UI under **Settings → Advanced** (stored locally on your instance), or you can set the `INTERNET_STATUS_TEST_URL` environment variable. When set, the environment variable always takes precedence over the UI-configured value. If neither is set, the built-in defaults above are used. ## About Security By design, Project NOMAD is intended to be open and available without hurdles — it includes no authentication. If you decide to connect your device to a local network after install (e.g. for allowing other devices to access its resources), you can block/open ports to control which services are exposed. **Will authentication be added in the future?** Maybe. It's not currently a priority, but if there's enough demand for it, we may consider building in an optional authentication layer in a future release to support use cases where multiple users need access to the same instance but with different permission levels (e.g. family use with parental controls, classroom use with teacher/admin accounts, etc.). We have a suggestion for this on our public roadmap, so if this is something you'd like to see, please upvote it here: https://roadmap.projectnomad.us/posts/1/user-authentication-please-build-in-user-auth-with-admin-user-roles For now, we recommend using network-level controls to manage access if you're planning to expose your NOMAD instance to other devices on a local network. NOMAD is not designed to be exposed directly to the internet, and we strongly advise against doing so unless you really know what you're doing, have taken appropriate security measures, and understand the risks involved. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome and appreciated! Please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines on how to contribute to the project. ### Testing Auto-Updates (Dry Run) The Command Center can automatically install **minor/patch** updates of itself during a configurable window, after a cool-off period, and only when pre-flight checks pass (sufficient disk for the new image, no downloads or app installs in progress). Major versions always require a manual update. Because exercising this logic with real version bumps is impractical, an Ace command runs the **entire decision pipeline without ever triggering an update**. Run it from the `admin/` directory: ```bash # 1) Deterministic scenario suite — no network, DB, or Docker required. # Proves every branch (major-only, cool-off, prerelease/draft, window wrap, …) # and exits non-zero on failure, so it's safe to wire into CI. node ace auto-update:dry-run --scenarios # 2) Simulate "what would happen if I were running 1.32.0 right now?" # against the LIVE GitHub releases feed and real pre-flight checks: node ace auto-update:dry-run --current=1.32.0 --force-enabled # 3) Fully of

name: ds-harness-remote
description: 基于 DeepSeek Harness 插件机制构建的远程访问方案，通过低延迟、端到端加密的 P2P 网络，支持使用 PC、移动端 和 Web 随时访问本地设备上的DSH 、CodeX、Cursor、Claude Code等工作区。 (Built on DeepSeek Harness plugins, this low-latency, end-to-end encrypted P2P solution lets PC, mobile, and web clients access local DSH, Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code workspaces.)
readme_content:
English  ·  中文  ·  日本語

## Connect once. Ready whenever you are. Continue using your DeepSeek Harness instance from a phone, computer, or browser. Return to the same Harness session from whichever device is with you. Harness keeps running on your work computer, with the same workspaces, tools, and project setup. DS Harness Remote is simply another window into that environment. The DeepSeek Harness desktop edition is supported. Install the latest release: `ds-harness-remote@0.6.4` ## Features - Access your local Harness instance remotely from the web, a PC, or a mobile device: DSH first, with Codex, Cursor, and Antigravity support too. - DeepSeek Harness Desktop is ready to use after installation, with its native interface and no separate desktop conversation UI. - Create workspaces, configure models, and switch conversation models with the same smooth workflow as local use. - No public listening port or public IP is required on the Harness Host. Connect from anywhere with internet access over a bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel. - Prefer P2P connections, use TURN relay nodes worldwide, and fall back to multiple Server Relays when needed. - Access workspace files, read-only previews, remote terminals, and authorized local development-service previews through the native Harness sidebar. - Remote Tool context injection supports Host and workspace discovery, Harness session creation and management, history reading, waiting for execution, interruption requests, and authorized file transfers. [Details](packages/plugin/README.md#remote-agent-tools). - Alongside DeepSeek Harness, access native workspaces for Codex, Cursor, Google Antigravity, Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, Harness Agent, and other tools through ACP integrations, with remote file browsing and terminals. - Clients are available across Android, iOS, Web, and native DSH. - Multiple clients can connect to the same Harness Host simultaneously, with RPC calls and streams isolated per connection. ## Supported clients | Client | Form | Status | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DSH Desktop plugin | Remote sidebar | Supported | Install `ds-harness-remote@0.6.4`; this computer can also be the Host | | Web | Browser page | Supported | Open [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn); reuses the native Harness interface | | Android | Native app | Supported | Download the APK from [Releases](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/releases/latest); see the [Android guide](apps/android/README.md) | | DSH Go | A standout app by ccch1mneyyy | Supported | See [ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go: an Android client for DeepSeek Harness. Run it directly on your phone or control DSH on your computer remotely.](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go) | | iOS | TestFlight beta | Beta | Not publicly released; see [issue #20](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20) | | Browser extension | Chrome | Entry point only | Exchanges an already signed-in Web authorization for a separate device credential, lists online Hosts and opens the same-origin Remote Web; it does not host a conversation UI | | dsh-TUI | Terminal-only CLI | Planned | Integration is not part of this release and returns in a later version; the installer never creates a Web service for it automatically | | Linux | Cloud server | Supported | Sign in on the [official website](https://dsh.r2049.cn/) to install with one command. | Several clients can connect to the same Host at once; RPC calls and streams are isolated per connection. ## Install ### DeepSeek Harness Desktop support Open **Extensions / Plugin management** in DeepSeek Harness Desktop, choose installation from npm, and enter this package: `ds-harness-remote@0.6.4` Restart Desktop afterward. Its official `dsh` launcher can also install the pinned package with `dsh plugin --profile desktop add -w ds-harness-remote@0.6.4`. On DSH 0.2.2+, npm installations support version checks and updates in Plugin management, with an attempt to restore the previous version if hot updating fails. GitHub and local link installations must switch to npm first; see [online updates](docs/installation.md#online-updates-in-dsh-plugin-management). ### Linux one-command installation Visit [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn/), sign in, and obtain an installation authorization code to install with one command. ### Native Android client Keep conversations connected across multiple workspaces at once, and use **Bot mode**, powered by [Fei2411/DS-Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot). Download the latest APK from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/releases/latest), and sign in to the same account to see your Hosts. ## DSH Go — DeepSeek Harness in your pocket: run it locally on your phone or control your computer remotely. [ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go) has built-in support for the ds-harness-remote protocol. You can run DeepSeek Harness locally on your phone or connect to your computer remotely. After installing the ds-harness-remote plugin in DSH Go on your phone, you can also connect to the phone’s DSH from your computer or the web and use Mobile Use seamlessly. ### iOS client - [Join the beta](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20) ## Quick start 1. Open **Remote** from the DeepSeek Harness sidebar. 2. Choose Zhihu, GitHub, or Google authorization, or sign in with an account and password. Account registration requires an invitation code; email the repository author to request one. 3. On another device, install the same plugin in DeepSeek Harness and sign in as described in steps 1–2. Alternatively, use Remote Web, iOS, Android, or DSH Go directly without installing a plugin. 4. Select an online Host, then choose an existing workspace or browse remote directories to open one. By default, Remote uses this project's hosted Server at [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn). For self-hosting, use the repository's [minimal Server](apps/server/README.md). The current version includes WebRTC LAN/P2P/TURN coordination (TURN requires your own coturn deployment) and an encrypted Relay Server, but does not provide the full hosted Remote Web experience. ## Screenshots ### Desktop On another computer, select an online Host and open its workspace. The workspace opens in the native Harness interface, with the active Host and encrypted connection status in the header.

To prevent this computer from controlling other Hosts, open the Host list at [https://dsh.r2049.cn/](https://dsh.r2049.cn/) and enable **Controlled only**. This device will no longer see other devices under your account, while Web and other clients can still connect to it remotely. ### Android Use text or image prompts, switch models, and access supported workspace files and terminals.

Mobile Settings includes a global **Compact conversations** switch, off by default and applied when a conversation is next opened. Supporting Hosts reduce historical tool details while preserving messages and tool status. Turn the setting off and reopen the conversation to load full history. ## How it works ```text DSH Desktop / Remote Web / Android ↔ authenticated, end-to-end encrypted channel Remote Plugin on the Host ↔ supported Harness or optional Codex workspace support Harness sessions/workspaces or Codex projects ``` The Harness Host does not need a public listening port. Connect from anywhere with internet access over ds-harness-remote’s bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel. The client switches to the selected Host’s native Harness API, keeping the original workspaces, tools, and permission flows on that computer. You can also edit Harness and plugin settings on the remote host. Available options depend on which settings Harness and each plugin expose through the official settings API. ## Experimental ACP workspaces The Host runs local ACP-capable Agents and forwards prompts, streamed replies, and approvals through ds-harness-remote. Each Agent keeps its own workspaces and sessions; only session translation for DSH is performed, without writing to Harness storage. Supported backends: - **Codex** — connects through App Server, using the shared workspace entry. - **Cursor** — connects through the CLI's ACP interface. - **Antigravity (AGY)** — connects through an adapter for its stream-json CLI. - **Pi Agent (experimental)** — automatically detected after installing and configuring Pi and `pi-acp`; can be disabled in settings. Tools run with Host-user permissions, without per-tool confirmation by default. - **OpenCode** — connects through `opencode acp`, with workspaces and history. Session archiving requires a build with the authenticated API; unarchive is not yet available. - **Claude** — connects through a locally authorized `claude-agent-acp`; enable it in settings. Supports text and approvals; images are not yet supported. - **Hermes** — connects through `hermes acp`; enable it in settings. Supports text, images, streamed output, approvals, and model selection. Claude and Hermes also support direct file and terminal access, subject to the Host's workspace boundaries and terminal settings. Setup and adapter development: [Agent workspace integration guide](docs/acp-integration.md). Model selection for Cursor, Claude, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, and AGY on Desktop/Android uses the Host's actual model catalog as determined by the Agent’s ACP interface. Reasoning effort options depend on what the backend provides. Cursor uses a separate process per session, so model changes do not affect other conversations. ## End-to-end encryption Harness business traffic is encrypted on the Client and decrypted only by the selected Host using the fixed `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` suite. Connections must pass both same-account membership and locally pin

name: zapfast
description: ZapFast: a fast, native WhatsApp client in Rust and egui
readme_content:
ZapFast

WhatsApp, native and fast.
A lightweight WhatsApp app for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

Download · Getting started · User guide · Contribute

ZapFast is a WhatsApp client written in Rust with [egui](https://www.egui.rs) and [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev), the framework behind a family of native desktop apps. It links to your phone as a companion device through [whatsapp-rust](https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust) and has no browser engine. In our Linux test it opens in under a second and uses about 200 MB of idle RAM, against 1.13 GB for WhatsApp Web. [See the measurements](https://zapfast.rocks/benchmarks/). The interface is available in English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Dutch, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Spanish, and Turkish.
Watch ZapFast in action https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bf86b54-45fc-4add-8de7-c426c3cdad9b
[Features](#your-chats-on-your-desktop) · [Install](#install) · [Link your phone](#link-your-phone) · [Help](#guides-and-help) ## Your chats, on your desktop | Feature | What you can do | |---|---| | **Messages** | Send formatted text, replies, edits, reactions, forwards, pictures, files, stickers, GIFs, polls, and voice messages. | | **Media in the chat** | Play voice messages, videos, round video messages, GIFs, and animated stickers in place. | | **Your history** | Keep your chats in an encrypted archive on this computer, fetch older messages from your phone as you scroll, and export locally saved chat history as text or a ZIP with downloaded attachments. | | **Several numbers** | Link more than one WhatsApp number and switch between them in one window. | | **Desktop controls** | Use keyboard shortcuts, select and copy text across messages, and stay linked in the tray with notifications. | | **Themes** | Choose light, dark, system appearance, or custom colours. On Omarchy, follow your desktop theme. | | **Privacy** | Hide locked chats behind a code, or the whole window behind an app lock. Nothing goes to a server of ours. | ## Install | Platform | Installation | |---|---| | **macOS** | `brew install --cask crmne/tap/zapfast`, or [download the Mac app](https://zapfast.rocks/download/#macos). | | **Arch Linux** | `yay -S zapfast-bin` | | **Windows** | Choose your build on the [Download page](https://zapfast.rocks/download/#windows). | | **Other Linux** | Find Nix, AppImage, and other options on the [Download page](https://zapfast.rocks/download/#linux). | | **From source** | Follow [Getting started](https://zapfast.rocks/getting-started/) for dependencies and commands. | ## Link your phone 1. Open ZapFast. It shows a QR code. 2. On your phone, open WhatsApp, then **Settings**, **Linked devices**, **Link a device**, and scan the code. Or click **Link with phone number** and enter the eight-character code on your phone. 3. Your recent chats arrive from the phone. Older messages follow as you scroll up. The link survives restarts, and your phone does not need to stay online to read what ZapFast has already stored. See [Getting started](https://zapfast.rocks/getting-started/) for the full walkthrough and [How it links](https://zapfast.rocks/how-it-links/) for the details. ## Guides and help The complete guide lives at **[zapfast.rocks](https://zapfast.rocks/)**. | You want to… | Read | |---|---| | Know what ZapFast does and does not do yet | [What is ZapFast?](https://zapfast.rocks/what-is-zapfast/) | | Link your phone or build from source | [Getting started](https://zapfast.rocks/getting-started/) | | Learn messages, stickers, polls, and shortcuts | [Using ZapFast](https://zapfast.rocks/using-zapfast/) | | Find settings, stored files, encryption, the app lock, and updates | [Settings and files](https://zapfast.rocks/settings-and-files/) | | Make your own theme | [Making a theme](https://zapfast.rocks/themes/) | | Understand what stays on this computer | [How it links](https://zapfast.rocks/how-it-links/) | | Understand account risk | [Account safety](https://zapfast.rocks/what-is-zapfast/#account-safety) | | Report a bug or propose a feature | Read [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md), then use the [issue forms](https://github.com/crmne/zapfast/issues/new/choose). | ## Contributing Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening an issue or pull request. To look at the interface without a WhatsApp account, run: ```sh cargo run --features demo -- --demo ``` [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) describes the architecture, [DEMO.md](DEMO.md) the demo pages, screenshots, and recorded tours, and [PACKAGING.md](PACKAGING.md) releases and packages. Native notifications use Fastframe on Linux, macOS and Windows. ZapFast keeps its account/chat routing, privacy settings, notification limits and sound previews. Clicks open the announced message; reading a chat withdraws its tracked notifications. OS permissions and notification presentation still apply. ## More native apps **Want Spotify just as fast and native?** [Spotifast](https://spotifast.rocks) is ZapFast's sibling. Both are built on [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev). ## Acknowledgements ZapFast uses [whatsapp-rust](https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust), [egui](https://www.egui.rs), [fastframe](https://fastframe.dev), the [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) typeface and Noto Color Emoji (OFL), and [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) icons (ISC), also used for the chat wallpaper doodles. The notification sounds are [Pidgin](https://pidgin.im)'s, under the GPL-2.0 (see `assets/sounds/`). ZapFast is an unofficial client and is not affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta. Using an unofficial client may be against WhatsApp's terms of service and could get an account suspended. Use it at your own risk. WhatsApp is a trademark of WhatsApp LLC. Licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). ## Star history
